feasibility.executiveSummary: The hybrid economy + two-tier civilization design is FEASIBLE and requires only moderate C# work. The lobby toggle pattern (Q1) exists and is production-ready. Heterogeneous capturable structures (Q2) can be built from stock traits via mod-data alone using existing Capturable/INotifyCapture patterns. Ore value restoration (Q3) is a one-line YAML change. Campaign persistence (Q4) is the hard blocker—OpenRA campaigns do NOT persist any state between missions; adding this requires either new C# infrastructure or hacky Lua workarounds. Structure upgrade ladders (Q5) can reuse Transforms/TransformOnCapture as mod-data.
keyFindings: LOBBY TOGGLE: Fully implemented. LobbyOptionsLogic + ILobbyOptions interface + LobbyBooleanOption + World.LobbyInfo.GlobalSettings pattern handles this. MapOptions.cs and CrateSpawner.cs are production examples. Traits can condition on toggle via RequiresCondition + GrantConditionOnPrerequisite or simply check GlobalSettings in INotifyCreated.

HETEROGENEOUS STRUCTURES: Stock traits exist for EVERY desired effect: CashTrickler (income), RevealsShroud (vision), GivesBuildableArea (buildable area unlock), RepairsUnits (repair nearby), Production (unit production from building), ProvidesPrerequisite + GrantConditionOnPrerequisite (tech tree unlocks/powers). Capturable trait + INotifyCapture interface allows triggers on ownership change. No new C# needed—pure mod-data composition.

CONCRETE TRAIT REUSE: CashTrickler (RequiresCondition + owner condition), RevealsShroud + RevealsShroudMultiplier (conditional range), GivesBuildableArea (conditional on owner), RepairsUnits (paused when disabled), Production (with conditional output), GpsDot (CNC mod, requires a watcher elsewhere), ProvidesPrerequisite (triggers tech unlock when enabled). All support RequiresCondition gates.

ORE VALUE: Trivial. ResourceValues in PlayerResources.Info (mods/ra/rules/player.yaml) controls ore/gem cash-per-unit. Phase 0 already proved this: set Ore: 0 disables harvesters. Tune Ore: 12-15 (vs default 25) to make territory ~30-50% of economy.

CAMPAIGN PERSISTENCE: THE CRITICAL GAP. OpenRA campaigns are stateless chains of independent missions. No mechanism for carrying player upgrades, tech tree, or nation development across missions. Each mission.yaml map is self-contained; Lua scripts only run within that mission's frame. mods/ra/missions.yaml is just a sequencing list. To add persistence requires: (1) New C# trait(s) that serialize/deserialize a 'CampaignProgress' blob at mission end and load it at mission start, or (2) Hacky Lua state stored on a neutral actor between maps (fragile), or (3) Custom mod-level mission-chaining logic. Estimate: 200–400 lines of new C# + mission UI integration.

STRUCTURE UPGRADES: Transforms.cs + TransformOnCapture.cs + conditional traits can achieve tier-ladder. Build 'tier1-structure', capture it, it transforms into 'tier2-structure' (via TransformOnCapture's IntoActor). Use GrantConditionOnPrerequisite to gate tier2 abilities until a captured tier1 exists. Pure mod-data; no C# needed.

EXISTING PATTERN PROOF: territory-economy.yaml (Phase 0) demonstrates the pattern perfectly: disables harvester income (ResourceValues), adds SupplyNode + CashTrickler with RequiresCondition gates. This is THE proof that conditional trait composition works.
recommendations: IMPLEMENT LOBBY TOGGLE IMMEDIATELY. Copy CrateSpawner's ILobbyOptions pattern (two-tier civ layer on/off). Map-level trait emits 'civlayer-enabled' condition to all owned actors at start. No blocking risk.

DESIGN CAPTURABLE STRUCTURE YAML NOW. Create five example archetypes: (1) Income node (CashTrickler+Capturable), (2) Vision node (RevealsShroud+Capturable), (3) Repair node (RepairsUnits+Capturable), (4) Production node (Production+Capturable), (5) Tech node (ProvidesPrerequisite+Capturable). Each requires only trait composition + RequiresCondition on owner. Prototype in mods/ra/rules/theater.yaml.

RESTORE ORE: Edit PlayerResources in mods/ra/rules/player.yaml. Test tunings: Ore: 0 (territory-only), Ore: 12 (60% territory), Ore: 15 (50% territory). Playtest to find 'feels like RA' value. Likely 12–15 to preserve harvester relevance without dominance.

FOR CAMPAIGN PERSISTENCE: Scope it as a separate task (spawn_task). Design required: (A) What data persists between missions? (resources, tech unlocks, units retained, captured structures/upgrades?), (B) UI flow — how does player see/manage persistent civilization? (pre-mission screen showing tech/resources?), (C) Save location — where does mission-chain state live? (player profile, per-campaign file?). Once scoped, implementation is ~200–400 LOC C# + Lua bindings.

STRUCTURE UPGRADE LADDER: Build mod-data prototype with three tiers: captured 'oil-derrick-t1' → (on capture) transforms into 'oil-derrick-t2' with +50% income → (some trigger: maybe a lobby option 't2-unlock' or time-based) transforms into 'oil-derrick-t3'. Use TransformOnCapture.IntoActor chaining. Test on a skirmish map with capturable structures.

PLAYTEST FAST: Create a single test map with 5–6 capturable nodes (mix types), baseline ore at 15, no supply chain. 1v1 skirmish. Measure 'does territory feel like a competitive objective equal to harvester defense?' If yes, iterate difficulty. If no, rebalance CashTrickler amounts or ore value.

REUSE EXISTING ART CEILING: All five node types can reskin Oil Derrick (OILB) with condition-based overlays (repair fx when damaged, cash-tick numbers when producing, etc.). Zero new sprites needed for prototype.
risks: Campaign persistence is non-trivial and may block the 'heavy civ layer' in CAMPAIGN mode. If player wants persistent nation development across 5+ mission chain, you MUST solve this. Currently it's architectural debt, not impossible but not free.

Conditional trait composition (RequiresCondition gates on everything) works but can become a readability/debugging nightmare if misapplied. YAML rules will balloon. Risk: mod maintainability suffers. Mitigation: create abstract base templates in rules (^CapturedIncomeNode: { ... }) and inherit, don't repeat.

Lobby toggle + conditional dispatch still requires that a trait runs at INotifyCreated to check GlobalSettings and grant the condition. If you forget the dispatcher trait, the feature is silent-broken. Risk: hidden bugs. Mitigation: test harness that verifies toggle actually gates the feature (mock a lobby toggle off, verify trait disabled).

Support power charge speedup: SupportPower.ChargeInterval is a static value; no ISupportPowerModifier interface exists (checked TraitsInterfaces.cs). To add 'captured structure speeds up support power charge,' you'd need a NEW C# trait (moderate, ~50 LOC) that hooks SupportPowerManager. Viable but not plug-and-play.

RepairsUnits + GivesBuildableArea work on the building that has them. RepairsUnits only heals units adjacent/in range. If you capture a 'repair node' but don't position it well, effect is dead. UX risk: captured structure is useful only if you think about placement. Mitigation: explicit UI messaging or guarantee nodes spawn in 'useful' positions (design maps carefully).

Transforms chaining (tier1 → tier2 → tier3 on captures) is possible but untested in production. Risk: animation/facing/health carryover bugs. The TransformOnCapture trait has `ForceHealthPercentage` field for this, but chaining multiple transforms may drop health unpredictably. Test thoroughly.

Territory income alone without harvesters: If players abuse 'take a few nodes, stop harvesting, grind out victory,' pacing may feel dead. Risk: matches degrade to attrition-grinding (opposite of the engagement problem you're solving). Mitigation: tune CashTrickler interval and amount aggressively; balance with building costs so income feels crisp, not slow.

## Question 1: LOBBY TOGGLE PATTERN — how ILobbyOptions checkboxes work

**FINDING: EXISTS and PRODUCTION-READY.**

File evidence:
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/MapOptions.cs` (lines 86–90): `ILobbyOptions.LobbyOptions(MapPreview map)` yields `LobbyBooleanOption("shortgame", ...)` — this is the interface contract.
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/CrateSpawner.cs` (lines 83–86): identical pattern for "crates" checkbox.
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox.cs` (lines 53–56): generic reusable checkbox that GRANTS PREREQUISITES when enabled — this is **exactly** what you need for "enable civ layer = unlock tech prerequisites."

**Concrete flow:**
1. Trait's `TraitInfo` implements `ILobbyOptions`.
2. `LobbyOptions()` method yields a `LobbyBooleanOption` with: ID ("civlayer"), label ("Civilization Layer"), enabled default, locked flag, visible flag.
3. At world creation, `INotifyCreated` reads `World.LobbyInfo.GlobalSettings.OptionOrDefault(id, default)` to fetch the player's lobby choice.
4. Trait stores the enabled state locally.
5. The trait can:
   - Directly gate behavior (e.g., `if (!enabled) return;` in a tick loop), OR
   - Grant a condition (`civlayer-enabled`) that other traits gate on via `RequiresCondition: civlayer-enabled`.

**HOW TO ENABLE FEATURES ON TOGGLE:**
- Use `GrantConditionOnPrerequisiteManager` pattern (LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox.cs lines 62–80): when the checkbox is on, it grants a prerequisite (or condition token) that flows into the tech tree.
- OR use a simpler custom trait: on Created, check toggle, call `self.GrantCondition("civlayer-enabled")` and store the token. When trait is disabled, revoke it.

**File path:** `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/LobbyOptionsLogic.cs` (the UI that renders these checkboxes on the lobby screen — you don't need to touch this, it auto-discovers ILobbyOptions).

**Effort:** mod-data only (create a new trait in rules YAML, e.g., `MatchCivilizationToggle: { ... }` inheriting from a base), ~0 lines of C#.

---

## Question 2: HETEROGENEOUS CAPTURABLE STRUCTURES — concrete reusable traits

**FINDING: ALL TRAITS EXIST. PURE MOD-DATA SOLUTION.**

The key insight: Capturable trait + INotifyCapture interface allows any trait to react to ownership change. Combine with existing conditional traits.

**Trait inventory:**

| Effect | Trait | File | How to use |
|--------|-------|------|-----------|
| **Income** | `CashTrickler` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/CashTrickler.cs` | Add `CashTrickler: { Interval: 25, Amount: 35, RequiresCondition: owned && supplied }` |
| **Vision** | `RevealsShroud` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/RevealsShroud.cs` | Add `RevealsShroud: { Range: 10c0, RequiresCondition: owned }`. Range is conditional via multipliers. |
| **Buildable area** | `GivesBuildableArea` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildings/GivesBuildableArea.cs` | Add `GivesBuildableArea: { AreaTypes: ["factory"], RequiresCondition: owned }`. Unlocks placement zones. |
| **Repair nearby** | `RepairsUnits` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/RepairsUnits.cs` | Add trait; it auto-repairs nearby units when they dock. Can pause via `RequiresCondition`. |
| **Unit production** | `Production` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Production.cs` | Add `Production: { Produces: ["Infantry"], RequiresCondition: owned }`. Building can produce units when captured. |
| **Tech unlock / Grant ability** | `ProvidesPrerequisite` + `GrantConditionOnPrerequisite` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProvidesPrerequisite.cs` and `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/GrantConditionOnPrerequisite.cs` | `ProvidesPrerequisite: { Prerequisite: "tech-radar", RequiresCondition: owned }` unlocks radar when captured; other actors with `GrantConditionOnPrerequisite: { Condition: "has-radar", Prerequisites: ["tech-radar"] }` gain radar overlay. |
| **GPS dot / Map reveal (CNC mod)** | `GpsDot` | `/OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Traits/GpsDot.cs` | Not in RA by default. Would need to port or create similar. Moderate effort (~50 LOC C#) if needed. |
| **Support power charge speedup** | ❌ MISSING | — | No ISupportPowerModifier exists. New C# trait required (~50–100 LOC). **Not trivial; flag as separate task.** |

**HOW CAPTURE TRIGGERS EFFECTS:**

`Capturable` trait exists at `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Capturable.cs`. It requires a `CaptureManager` and implements `INotifyCapture`. When captured:
1. All traits on the actor that implement `INotifyCapture` are notified.
2. `GivesCashOnCapture` (file: `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/GivesCashOnCapture.cs`) is a concrete example: it implements `INotifyCapture.OnCapture()` and grants cash to the new owner.

**TO GRANT A CONDITION ON CAPTURE:**
You need a custom trait implementing `INotifyCapture` that grants a condition. Example pseudo-YAML:
```yaml
GrantConditionOnCapture:
  Condition: owned
```
This trait would:
```csharp
public class GrantConditionOnCapture : INotifyCapture {
  int token = Actor.InvalidConditionToken;
  public void OnCapture(Actor self, Actor captor, Player oldOwner, Player newOwner, BitSet<CaptureType> captureTypes) {
    if (token != Actor.InvalidConditionToken)
      token = self.RevokeCondition(token);
    token = self.GrantCondition(Info.Condition);
  }
}
```

**BUT:** You can repurpose existing patterns. If you use `TransformOnCapture` (file: `/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/TransformOnCapture.cs`), the structure transforms into a new actor type on capture. That new type has any traits you want. Simpler for big transformations; less elegant for incremental changes.

**FILE PATHS (copy-pasta ready):**
- CashTrickler: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/CashTrickler.cs`
- RevealsShroud: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/RevealsShroud.cs`
- GivesBuildableArea: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildings/GivesBuildableArea.cs`
- RepairsUnits: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/RepairsUnits.cs`
- Production: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Production.cs`
- ProvidesPrerequisite: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProvidesPrerequisite.cs`
- GrantConditionOnPrerequisite: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/GrantConditionOnPrerequisite.cs`
- Capturable: `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Capturable.cs`
- GivesCashOnCapture (reference pattern): `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/GivesCashOnCapture.cs`

**Effort:** ~0 lines of C#. Create new rules YAML actors:
```yaml
INCOMENODE:
  Inherits: ^BaseBuilding
  Capturable: { Types: ["infantry"] }
  CashTrickler: { Amount: 50, Interval: 25, RequiresCondition: player-owned }
  RevealsShroud: { Range: 8c0, RequiresCondition: player-owned }
  # (and renderer + health traits)
```
Then a `GrantConditionOnCapture` trait (50 LOC C#) if you want incremental condition grants; otherwise TransformOnCapture existing structures.

## Question 4: CAMPAIGN PERSISTENCE — THE HARD ONE

**FINDING: NO MECHANISM EXISTS. ARCHITECTURAL GAP.**

OpenRA campaigns are **stateless chains**. Evidence:

1. **Mission structure** (`/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/missions.yaml`): Lists mission sequences by name. No state blob, no progression tracker.

2. **Mission map** (`/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/maps/allies-01/map.yaml`): Self-contained actors, starting cash, Lua script. No reference to previous mission state.

3. **Campaign Lua** (`/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/scripts/campaign.lua`): Generic helper functions (InitObjectives, ChooseRandomTarget, etc.). No persistence hooks.

4. **Mission browser** (`/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/MissionBrowserLogic.cs`, line 78): Comment says "TODO: this should be persistent across game sessions" — but it's only for UI state (selected difficulty), not game state.

5. **MissionData** (`/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/MissionData.cs`): Stores only briefing videos and FMV references. No campaign-level state.

6. **D2K campaigns** (e.g., `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/d2k/maps/harkonnen-09a/harkonnen09a.lua`): Hardcode upgrades at mission start via `Actor.Create("upgrade.barracks", ...)`. Not persisted; baked into each map's Lua.

**Why this is a blocker:**

If you want "player develops tech tree across 5 missions" or "captured oil derricks accumulate nation-level bonuses," you need:
1. **Serialization:** At mission end, save player tech tree, captured structures, nation XP, etc.
2. **State location:** Where does this live? Campaign profile? World actor? Player profile?
3. **Deserial at mission start:** Load previous state and apply to new mission.
4. **UI:** How does player see/manage persistent nation? Separate pre-mission screen?

**Current workaround (D2K model):** Hardcode each mission's starting upgrades/tech based on the mission sequence. E.g., if it's "mission 3," pre-spawn "upgrade.tech-buildings." Not dynamic; breaks if player loses tech.

**What you'd need to build:**

**Option A: Minimal (Lua-only hack, ~100 LOC Lua + some C# bindings)**
- At mission end, store a Lua table on a neutral actor: `campaign_progress = { tech_radar = true, oil_derricks_captured = 5, ... }`.
- On next mission, Lua script reads that table and re-applies tech/spawns structures.
- **Risk:** Fragile; if neutral actor dies or loads wrong, state lost.

**Option B: Proper (new C# trait, ~200–400 LOC C#)**
- New trait `CampaignPersistence` on world actor.
- At mission end, hook `INotifyGameEnd` to serialize player state (tech tree, actor IDs of captured structures, custom counters) to a JSON blob.
- On next mission, load blob and `GrantCondition()` for each tech, recreate or flag captured structures.
- Store blob in player profile or per-campaign file.
- **Requires:** Integration with mission loading flow (when? where?).

**Option C: Map-level parameters (moderate, ~50 LOC C#)**
- Pass lobby settings through map chain. E.g., `?previous_tech_radar=true&previous_ore_count=1500`.
- Next mission's Lua reads query params and applies.
- **Risk:** Limited to ~20 params; dirty workaround.

**Estimate:**
- **Scoping conversation:** 30 min (what persists? UI? save location?).
- **Option A (Lua hack):** 2–4 hours (test edge cases).
- **Option B (proper C# trait + mission UI integration):** 8–16 hours (design, implementation, testing).
- **Option C (query params):** 2–3 hours (simple but limited).

**Recommendation:** **DO NOT BUILD THIS FOR PHASE 0.** Flag as separate task. Focuses on MATCHES (main mode, non-persistent) first. CAMPAIGN persistence is a future phase.

---

## Question 5: STRUCTURE UPGRADE LADDER (tier progression)

**FINDING: DOABLE VIA TRANSFORMS + CONDITIONS. PURE MOD-DATA MOSTLY.**

**Pattern: Chain transformations on capture**

1. **Tier 1 (base captured structure):** `OILDERRICK-T1` inherits Capturable, adds some base income (CashTrickler).
2. **Tier 2:** `TransformOnCapture: { IntoActor: OILDERRICK-T2 }` on Tier 1. When captured, transforms into Tier 2 (same actor, or different).
3. **Tier 3:** Tier 2 has `TransformOnCapture: { IntoActor: OILDERRICK-T3 }` or a condition-based trigger (e.g., `Transforms: { IntoActor: OILDERRICK-T3 }` with `RequiresCondition: can-upgrade`).

**Concrete YAML example:**
```yaml
OILDERRICK-T1:
  Inherits: OILB
  Health: { HP: 1000 }
  Capturable: { Types: ["infantry"] }
  CashTrickler: { Amount: 35, Interval: 25, RequiresCondition: player-owned }
  TransformOnCapture:
    IntoActor: OILDERRICK-T2
    SkipMakeAnims: true

OILDERRICK-T2:
  Inherits: OILB
  Health: { HP: 1500 }
  Capturable: { Types: ["infantry"] }
  CashTrickler: { Amount: 70, Interval: 25, RequiresCondition: player-owned }
  Transforms:
    IntoActor: OILDERRICK-T3
    DeployCursor: upgrade
  GivesBuildableArea: { AreaTypes: ["factory"], RequiresCondition: player-owned }
```

**How to trigger upgrade from T2 to T3:**
- **Option 1:** Manual (player right-clicks building, selects "Upgrade"). Requires `IIssueOrder` on Transforms trait (already supported).
- **Option 2:** Automatic on condition. Add `GrantConditionOnPrerequisite: { Condition: upgrade-available, Prerequisites: ["tech-upgrade-oil-t3"] }` to Tier 2. When player unlocks tech, auto-deploys (calls Transforms.GetTransformActivity()).
- **Option 3:** Time-based. Trait tracks ticks; at N ticks, auto-transform. Need custom ~50 LOC C# trait.

**File reference:**
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Transforms.cs` (lines 22–69): trait definition, CanDeploy(), GetTransformActivity().
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/TransformOnCapture.cs`: auto-transform on capture.

**Effort:**
- Three actor definitions in YAML: ~30 lines.
- If using condition-based auto-upgrade: no C#.
- If using time-based or custom logic: 50–100 LOC C#.

**Gotcha:** When Tier 1 transforms to Tier 2, does it keep health? ForceHealthPercentage field in TransformOnCapture (file, line 25) controls this. Default 0 means preserve current HP %. Use ForceHealthPercentage: 50 to set to 50% of new tier's max.

---

## SUMMARY TABLE

| Question | Status | Effort | Blocker? |
|----------|--------|--------|----------|
| 1. Lobby toggle | EXISTS (CrateSpawner pattern) | 0 C#, ~10 lines YAML | No |
| 2. Heterogeneous structures | EXISTS (trait composition) | 0–50 C# (GrantConditionOnCapture), ~50 lines YAML | No |
| 3. Ore value tuning | TRIVIAL | 1 line YAML | No |
| 4. Campaign persistence | MISSING | 200–400 C# (Option B) | **YES** (flag as future) |
| 5. Upgrade ladder | DOABLE (Transforms) | 0–100 C# (if auto-upgrade), ~30 lines YAML | No |

**For PHASE 1 (MATCHES focus):** Questions 1–3, 5 are go. Question 4 is out-of-scope (non-persistent match civ layer only).

structures.executiveSummary:
A roster of 11 heterogeneous capturable territory structures for THEATER's hybrid map layer, deliberately split so that only THREE print or grant direct cash and the rest pay in CAPABILITY (vision, repair, detection, forward production, support-power charge, defense) or AMPLIFY the existing ore loop rather than running a parallel wallet. The design intent is to seed a Red Alert map with 6-10 of these (a curated subset per map, not all 11), each pulling a player's attention for a DIFFERENT reason, so the "expand-to-ore vs. protect-harvesters vs. fight-for-control" triangle stays live and the map never collapses into one repeated control point — the exact failure the Phase-0 derrick-only playtest exposed.

Grounding: RA's own canon capturables (Oil Derrick/OILB, Hospital/HOSP, Forward Command/FCOM, Tech Center/TECN, Bio Lab/BIO, Radar Dome, Communications Center) are the art and lore anchors; balance/readability patterns are lifted from C&C Generals tech buildings (the cleanest 1:1 trait map: derrick=income, refinery=cheaper vehicles, hospital=heal, repair bay=repair, reinforcement pad=free units), Dawn of War's TIERED Listening-Post-on-a-point (capture is step one, fortifying/upgrading deepens the payoff and the defensive investment), Company of Heroes' specialized fuel/munitions points (a captured point boosts a SPECIFIC resource stream, not a generic one) plus its decay/cutoff logic, and BFME outposts/build-plots (neutral plots you conquer to expand your developable footprint). Almost everything is mod-data over existing OpenRA traits; only the support-power-charge booster and the resource-yield aura need a small (~40-line) ConditionalTrait each.

THE KEY ANTI-SECOND-WALLET MECHANISM: economic structures attach a player-scoped ProvidesPrerequisite on capture, which flips a ConditionalTrait multiplier (ResourceValueMultiplier / ProductionCostMultiplier) ON. They make YOUR HARVESTERS WORTH MORE or YOUR FACTORIES CHEAPER instead of trickling independent cash — so they reward you only if you are still running the sacred harvester loop, structurally welding territory to the ore economy instead of replacing it.
structures.designPrinciples:
1. HYBRID BY HEADCOUNT: of 11 structures, only 3 touch cash directly (one classic trickle Derrick kept for nostalgia/tempo, plus two AMPLIFIERS that boost ore value/factory cost — not flat income). The other 8 pay in capability. A map ships 6-10 of them, so on any given map the cash-printers are a minority of objectives. This is the structural fix for the "second wallet / control-point game" the user rejected.

2. AMPLIFY, DON'T DUPLICATE THE WALLET: economic structures hook the EXISTING ore loop. ResourceValueMultiplier raises the cash-per-ore your refineries pay out; ProductionCostMultiplier discounts what you build. Their value is ZERO if you've stopped harvesting/producing — so they reinforce the harvester triangle (expand-protect-fight) instead of letting you skip it. This is the CoH "specialized fuel point" idea (boost a specific stream) crossed with the canon RA economy.

3. EVERY STRUCTURE PULLS FOR A DIFFERENT REASON: income, vision, mobile-repair, detection, forward spawn point, support-power tempo, area denial/defense, ore-field enrichment, build-radius expansion, prerequisite/tech unlock, heal. No two share a primary verb, so a player scanning the map sees a menu of distinct objectives, not N copies of one flag. This is the explicit antidote to the repeated-control-point drift.

4. CAPTURE IS STEP ONE, NOT THE WHOLE STORY (Dawn of War tiering): the most contested structures support an OPTIONAL upgrade/fortify tier (turret, deeper bonus) funded by the owner, so holding ground becomes an ongoing investment decision and a juicier re-capture target — depth without analysis-paralysis because it's all one or two on-map clicks.

5. REUSE OVER REBUILD: ~9 of 11 are pure MiniYAML on stock traits (Capturable, CaptureManager, CashTrickler, RevealsShroud, DetectCloaked, GivesBuildableArea, BaseProvider, Production, RepairsUnits, ProvidesPrerequisite, GrantConditionOnPrerequisite, ResourceValueMultiplier, ProductionCostMultiplier, ProximityExternalCondition, OwnerLostAction). Only TWO need new C#: a support-power ChargeRateMultiplier (no stock charge modifier exists) and a SeedsResource/yield aura tweak enough to stay deterministic. Art ceiling respected: every entry reskins an existing RA structure (OILB, HOSP, FCOM, TECN, BIO, DOME, radar/comms, fixit/repair bay sprites).

6. DETERMINISM-SAFE: all effects are integer multipliers, condition flips, tick-interval tricklers, or proximity scans already used in shipping sim code. No float/Random/wall-clock introduced. The two new traits are ConditionalTrait subclasses mirroring ResourceValueMultiplier exactly.

7. TOGGLEABLE & NON-PERSISTENT IN MATCHES: the whole layer is opt-in per the existing crates/bounty lobby-checkbox pattern (mirrors territory-economy.yaml already being opt-in via map Rules:), and nothing persists past match end. The heavier persistent civ lean is reserved for campaign, out of scope here.

structures.name: Oil Derrick (OILB) — kept as the lone classic trickle
structures.raBasis: RA's canonical Oil Derrick (OILB) — already in mods/ra/rules/civilian.yaml with CashTrickler 100/375t plus GivesCashOnCapture 100. The C&C lineage's signature capturable.
structures.effect: Flat passive income: a modest cash trickle while owned (e.g. ~100 every ~15s) plus a small capture bounty. Deliberately the ONLY pure-trickle structure in the set, and tuned low so it's tempo/snowball seasoning, not a strategy unto itself.
structures.whyContested: Instant, no-strings cash — the universally legible objective and the early-game tempo magnet. It's the baseline every player understands, but because it's a minority of one among 11, grabbing derricks alone can't win: it nudges your curve, it doesn't replace harvesting. Keeping exactly one preserves RA nostalgia without recreating the rejected derrick-only economy.
structures.engineReuse: Already implemented: CashTrickler + GivesCashOnCapture + Capturable + CaptureManager + CapturableProgressBar/Blink + OwnerLostAction(ChangeOwner) + GpsDot. Zero new code; just include OILB and tune CashTrickler.Amount/Interval down.

structures.name: Refinery Concession (Tech Oil Refinery) — ore-value amplifier
structures.raBasis: Maps C&C Generals' Tech Oil Refinery (cheaper vehicles) onto RA's economy; reskins OILB or a TECN/industrial sprite. Lore: a captured processing plant that upgrades how much your ore is worth.
structures.effect: While owned, raises the cash-per-ore your refineries pay out (e.g. +15-25% resource value) via a player-scoped condition that enables ResourceValueMultiplier. It AMPLIFIES the harvester loop — pays nothing if you aren't harvesting/unloading.
structures.whyContested: It is the literal embodiment of the corrected thesis: it makes your existing harvesters richer rather than printing a second income. Worth fighting for in proportion to how hard you're harvesting, so it tightens the expand-vs-protect tension instead of bypassing it. Denying it to the enemy hurts THEIR ore loop, not a side wallet.
structures.engineReuse: ProvidesPrerequisite@refinery (owner-scoped, on capture) -> player GrantConditionOnPrerequisite -> player-level ResourceValueMultiplier{Modifier:120, RequiresCondition} (stock trait, already ConditionalTrait). Capturable/CaptureManager/OwnerLostAction as usual. No new C#.

structures.name: Foundry / War Plant (Tech Factory) — production-cost amplifier
structures.raBasis: C&C Generals Tech Oil Refinery's 'cheaper construction' role, given an industrial-foundry skin (reskin TECN or a warfactory-adjacent civ building). Complements the Refinery Concession so the two economic amplifiers pull differently.
structures.effect: While owned, discounts unit/vehicle production cost (e.g. -10-15%) via player-scoped ProductionCostMultiplier. Spends your ore further rather than generating ore — an economy amplifier on the OUTPUT side, not a wallet.
structures.whyContested: Rewards aggression and re-buy tempo: the player actively pumping units gets the most from it, so it pulls the 'fight for map control' corner of the triangle. Like the Refinery it's worthless if you're idle, which keeps it welded to actually playing RA rather than camping a cash point.
structures.engineReuse: ProvidesPrerequisite@foundry -> GrantConditionOnPrerequisite -> ProductionCostMultiplier{Modifier:88, RequiresCondition} (stock ConditionalTrait). No new C#.

structures.name: Prospecting Station — ore-field enrichment node (CoH fuel-point analogue)
structures.raBasis: No exact RA canon; closest is the Tiberium-spike/derrick idea reskinned as a survey rig (OILB/IND sprite). Inspired directly by CoH's specialized fuel/munitions point: a captured node that boosts a SPECIFIC resource near it, and by D2k spice-bloom seeding.
structures.effect: Enriches the ORE FIELD around it — slowly thickens/regrows nearby ore cells while owned (a gentle SeedsResource-style aura), making that patch denser and longer-lived. The payoff is realized only by sending harvesters there.
structures.whyContested: This is the cleanest expression of 'territory AUGMENTS harvesting': capturing it makes a contested ore patch the richest on the map, forcing the enemy to choose between contesting your now-juicy field or ceding economy. It physically MOVES the harvester fight onto a captured tile — exactly the triangle the user wants, with harvesting still front-and-center.
structures.engineReuse: Mostly stock: SeedsResource (used by D2k spice) gated by the captured/enabled condition, scoped to surrounding cells; Capturable/CaptureManager. Needs a SMALL new ConditionalTrait wrapper (~40 lines) to gate SeedsResource by owner-condition and cap regrowth deterministically (integer cell-tick, no Random) — or a thin proximity ResourceValueMultiplier variant if seeding proves too swingy.

structures.name: Watchtower / Listening Post — vision & forward sight (DoW tiered)
structures.raBasis: RA's Communications Center / lookout role; reskin the small radar/comms or a guard-tower civ sprite. Named after Dawn of War's Listening Post to signal the tiered-upgrade idea.
structures.effect: Reveals a generous radius of shroud around itself while owned (forward vision over a chokepoint or ore route). Optional owner-funded TIER upgrade extends the reveal range and adds a light turret (a la DoW fortifying a strategic point).
structures.whyContested: Pure information advantage at a key crossing — sees enemy harvester routes, pushes, and flanks before they arrive. Prints no cash, so it's a textbook 'power, not wallet' objective; whoever holds it fights with the lights on. The tier upgrade makes holding it an escalating investment and a tastier re-capture prize.
structures.engineReuse: Stock: RevealsShroud (Range, with the GAPGEN variant already patterned in FCOM/HOSP) + Capturable + CaptureManager + OwnerLostAction. Tier upgrade = GrantConditionOnPrerequisite toggling a wider RevealsShroud + enabling an Armament/turret trait. No new C#.

structures.name: Field Hospital (HOSP) — infantry heal aura
structures.raBasis: RA's canonical Hospital (HOSP) in civilian.yaml; C&C Generals Tech Hospital (heals friendly infantry). Direct canon reuse.
structures.effect: Heals friendly infantry — either on entry (stock HOSP dock-heal) or, better for a contested point, a continuous heal AURA on nearby friendly infantry while owned.
structures.whyContested: Turns a forward position into a sustainable infantry anchor: bodies that would die in a normal RA trade instead recycle and hold the line. Pulls the infantry-heavy 'protect/fight' corner. No cash; its value is purely staying power, and it's most worth fighting over right where the fighting already is.
structures.engineReuse: Stock: HOSP already exists (Capturable, RevealsShroud, InstantlyRepairable). For the aura version use ProximityExternalCondition granting a 'being-healed' external condition to allied infantry, paired with the existing health-regen/condition plumbing. Minimal-to-no new C#.

structures.name: Service Depot / Repair Bay (FIX) — vehicle repair point (DoW tiered)
structures.raBasis: RA's Service Depot (FIX) / C&C Generals Tech Repair Bay (repairs friendly vehicles). Reskin the repair-bay sprite as a neutral capturable.
structures.effect: Repairs friendly vehicles that dock (stock RepairsUnits resupply model). Optional forward variant: a slow proximity self-repair aura so armored pushes self-sustain near it. Capturing denies the enemy a forward patch-up point.
structures.whyContested: Forward armor repair changes the math of every tank trade near it — you commit damaged vehicles you'd otherwise pull back. It's the vehicle counterpart to the Hospital and pulls map control toward whoever owns the forward repair. Cashless capability; deny-value is as high as use-value.
structures.engineReuse: Stock: RepairsUnits (PausableConditionalTrait, dock/resupply model) + DockHost/DockClientManager already used by FIX + Capturable/CaptureManager. Proximity-aura variant uses ProximityExternalCondition + a self-repair condition. Essentially no new C#.

structures.name: Radar Outpost (Tech Bunker / Spy Sat node) — detection + sensor sweep
structures.raBasis: RA Radar Dome (DOME) + Spy Satellite/GPS lineage; C&C Generals 'reveal/scan' tech. Reskin DOME or the comms dish. Distinct from the Watchtower: this one DETECTS, not just reveals.
structures.effect: Grants cloak/submarine DETECTION over an area (DetectCloaked) and optionally a periodic radar ping/reveal. Pairs with RA's stealth units (subs, spies, cloaked tech) so owning it neutralizes a whole enemy playstyle in its zone.
structures.whyContested: A hard counter to stealth/sub harassment that's LOCATIONAL — you only get detection where you hold the node. Whoever owns it strips the enemy's cloak advantage over that lane; losing it re-opens you to invisible raids on your harvesters. Sharp, asymmetric pull distinct from plain vision.
structures.engineReuse: Stock: DetectCloaked (Range, Types) + RevealsShroud + Capturable + CaptureManager. Periodic ping via a light scripted reveal or GpsDot-style trait. No new C# (DetectCloaked is a standard structure trait).

structures.name: Forward Command Post (FCOM) — build-radius expansion / forward staging
structures.raBasis: RA's Forward Command (FCOM) in civilian.yaml — it already carries GivesBuildableArea + BaseProvider. Also echoes BFME outposts/build-plots (capture a neutral plot to expand where you can build).
structures.effect: Extends your BUILDABLE AREA around it (GivesBuildableArea) and acts as a BaseProvider, letting you construct/expand forward from the captured point — projecting your base toward the front. Optionally a forward MCV-free staging anchor.
structures.whyContested: This is the 'develop the ground / Foothold-not-Empire' verb in physical form: capturing it lets you grow your developable footprint into contested territory, the closest thing to a Civ-style settle on the battlefield. It's spatial power, not cash — it changes WHERE you can play, which reshapes the whole map.
structures.engineReuse: Already implemented on FCOM: GivesBuildableArea{AreaTypes:building} + BaseProvider{Range} + Capturable + CaptureManager + OwnerLostAction(ChangeOwner) + PauseOnCondition(being-captured). Pure data reuse; no new C#.

structures.name: Reinforcement Depot (Tech Reinforcement Pad) — forward production / free units
structures.raBasis: C&C Generals Tech Reinforcement Pad (periodic free vehicles); RA forward-barracks flavor. Reskin a hangar/depot or TECN sprite.
structures.effect: While owned, periodically spawns a small free unit at the structure (ProduceActorPower / Production on a charge timer), OR acts as a forward Production exit so units you build arrive at the front. Tuned to drip cheap units, not flood.
structures.whyContested: A forward spawn point compresses reinforcement travel time — the holder reinforces the front instantly while the enemy walks across the map. That tempo edge in a fast RA game is decisive at a chokepoint. The free-unit drip is capability/tempo, not a cash stream, so it dodges the wallet trap while still feeling like 'income.'
structures.engineReuse: Stock: Production + RallyPoint + Reservable (forward-exit variant) OR a ProduceActorPower/SpawnActorPower on a ChargeInterval (free-unit variant), both gated by the captured/enabled condition + Capturable/CaptureManager. No new C# for the production-exit version; the timed-spawn version reuses existing SupportPower spawn traits.

structures.name: Tech Center / Relay (TECN) — support-power charge accelerator + tech unlock
structures.raBasis: RA's Technology Center (TECN/TECN2) in civilian.yaml + Communications Center lineage; the 'relic point' tier of DoW (the rare, decisive map objective). The single most contested node on a map.
structures.effect: Two coupled effects while owned: (1) ACCELERATES your support-power charge (e.g. -20% charge time) for powers like Chronosphere/Iron Curtain/airstrike — a CAPABILITY/tempo boost, not cash; and (2) grants a PREREQUISITE that unlocks a piece of tech you otherwise can't build. Hybrid because it touches both your power economy (faster superweapons) and your tech tree, but never prints money.
structures.whyContested: The map's 'relic': it bends your highest-impact swing (the next Iron Curtain push, the early Chrono) AND opens a tech option. That dual, game-defining pull makes it the structure both players orient the match around — the deliberate single high-stakes objective that anchors the map without being a cash point. Tuned as the rarest spawn (1 per map).
structures.engineReuse: Tech unlock = stock ProvidesPrerequisite@tech (owner-scoped) feeding normal Buildable Prerequisites (exactly how RA tech buildings already gate units). Charge accel needs a SMALL new C# trait: a ChargeRateMultiplier ConditionalTrait implementing an ISupportPowerChargeModifier hook on SupportPower (no stock charge modifier exists today — ReloadDelayMultiplier is the closest analogue to copy, ~40 lines). Everything else (Capturable/CaptureManager/condition wiring) is stock.

structures.detail:
PLACEMENT / MAP RECIPE (so the triangle stays live): a THEATER map should ship roughly 6-10 of these, never all 11 and never many copies of one. A balanced spread is ~2-3 economic-AMPLIFIER nodes (Refinery Concession, Foundry, Prospecting Station) placed near or between ore fields so the harvester fight and the control fight overlap; ~1 classic Oil Derrick near a contested midpoint for early tempo; ~3-4 power nodes (Watchtower, Hospital, Repair Bay, Radar Outpost, Reinforcement Depot, Forward Command) spread across lanes/chokes so each lane has a distinct reason to push; and exactly ONE Tech Center/Relay as the central high-stakes relic. This guarantees no two adjacent objectives reward the same verb — the explicit cure for the repeated-control-point drift.

WHY THIS FIXES THE PHASE-0 FAILURE (concrete): the rejected prototype set ore to 0 and made derricks 100% of income, so harvesting was meaningless and the map became one repeated cash flag. This roster inverts both: (a) ore stays the major income (50-70%, untouched harvester loop), and (b) of 11 structures only the lone Derrick prints independent cash — the other two 'economic' ones (Refinery Concession, Foundry) are MULTIPLIERS on your existing ore/production, so they reward harvesting harder instead of replacing it, and the Prospecting Station literally enriches an ore FIELD you must still harvest. The remaining 8 pay in capability, so the map is a menu of distinct objectives.

KEY ENGINE WIRING PATTERN (reused for every economic/buff structure): captured structure carries an owner-scoped ProvidesPrerequisite (RA tech buildings already do this — see ProvidesPrerequisite@buildingname throughout civilian.yaml). The owning PLAYER carries GrantConditionOnPrerequisite (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/GrantConditionOnPrerequisite.cs) which grants a condition while that prerequisite is held. That condition's RequiresCondition then enables a player-level ConditionalTrait multiplier: ResourceValueMultiplier (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Multipliers/ResourceValueMultiplier.cs — IResourceValueModifier, modifies cash paid when ore is delivered to a refinery) or ProductionCostMultiplier. Capture loss flips the prerequisite off and the buff vanishes — clean, deterministic, no persistence. This is the single pattern that makes territory AUGMENT (not duplicate) the economy.

NEW CODE REQUIRED (honest accounting — this is mostly mod-data): only TWO small traits. (1) A support-power ChargeRateMultiplier ConditionalTrait for the Tech Center — there is no stock charge-rate modifier (SupportPower.cs exposes ChargeInterval but nothing modifies it), so add an ISupportPowerChargeModifier hook on SupportPower and a ConditionalTrait that returns an integer % while enabled, mirroring ReloadDelayMultiplier.cs almost line-for-line (~40 lines + a one-line hook in SupportPower's charge tick). (2) A gated/owner-scoped SeedsResource wrapper (or a capped proximity yield aura) for the Prospecting Station, so ore enrichment is deterministic (integer cell-tick budget, no Random) and disappears when the node is lost. Everything else — Capturable, CaptureManager, CapturableProgressBar/Blink, OwnerLostAction(ChangeOwner), CashTrickler, GivesCashOnCapture, RevealsShroud, DetectCloaked, GivesBuildableArea, BaseProvider, Production, RallyPoint, Reservable, RepairsUnits, ProximityExternalCondition, ProvidesPrerequisite, GrantConditionOnPrerequisite, ResourceValueMultiplier, ProductionCostMultiplier, ProduceActorPower/SpawnActorPower — is shipping engine code already used by RA structures.

DAWN-OF-WAR TIERING (optional depth, opt-in): the Watchtower, Repair Bay, and Tech Center support an owner-funded upgrade tier — capture is step one, fortifying is an ongoing investment (wider range + a light turret via a granted condition toggling extra RevealsShroud/Armament traits). This adds the 'develop the ground' civ verb at the structure level with one on-map click, no menus, and makes a held node a richer re-capture target — depth without analysis-paralysis. It can be left out of a first prototype and bolted on later.

ART CEILING RESPECTED: every entry is a reskin of an existing RA structure sprite — OILB (Derrick, Refinery Concession, Prospecting Station), HOSP (Hospital), FIX/repair-bay (Repair Bay), DOME/comms dish (Radar Outpost, Watchtower), FCOM (Forward Command), TECN/TECN2 (Foundry, Tech Center), hangar/depot (Reinforcement Depot). No new 32-facing art required for a prototype; differentiation is by tooltip, GpsDot string, and effect.

RELEVANT FILES (all absolute): /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/rules/civilian.yaml (OILB L518, HOSP L176, FCOM L127, BIO L484, TECN L102 — the capturable templates to inherit/reskin); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/rules/territory-economy.yaml (the existing opt-in territory layer and the CTRL/SupplyNode pattern to mirror for the lobby-toggle wiring); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Multipliers/ResourceValueMultiplier.cs (the ore-amplify mechanism); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Multipliers/ReloadDelayMultiplier.cs (template to copy for the new ChargeRateMultiplier); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/SupportPowers/SupportPower.cs (ChargeInterval — needs the one-line charge-modifier hook); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/GrantConditionOnPrerequisite.cs and /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProvidesPrerequisite.cs (capture->player-buff wiring); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/ProximityExternalCondition.cs (heal/repair auras); /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/RepairsUnits.cs, .../Buildings/BaseProvider.cs, .../DetectCloaked.cs, .../SeedsResource.cs, .../Production.cs (the capability traits). Reference designs that shaped the roster: C&C Generals tech buildings (cncnz.com/games/generals/tech-buildings, cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Tech_building), Dawn of War Listening Post tiering and requisition decay (dow.fandom.com/wiki/Requisition), Company of Heroes specialized fuel/munitions points and cutoff/decay (companyofheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Resources, /wiki/Strategic_Point), BFME outposts/build-plots (bfme.fandom.com/wiki/Outpost).

OUT OF SCOPE (per constraints): the cuttable supply-chain mechanic is on hold (the territory-economy.yaml SupplyNetwork exists but I did not design around it here); persistent cross-mission civ development is campaign-only; and the lobby-toggle/non-persistence is assumed to follow the existing crates/bounty checkbox pattern rather than being specified trait-by-trait.

campaign-meta.executiveSummary: THEATER's campaign needs a persistent "civilization you develop" without the Civ/Stellaris management tax. The cleanest model from the precedents is Dawn of War: Dark Crusade crossed with XCOM and Homeworld, NOT Total War or Stellaris. The winning pattern across every successful precedent is the same: persist a SMALL, EMOTIONALLY-LEGIBLE set of things the player named and grew (a hero, a veteran roster, a developed home region, a faction identity/tech), and HARD-RESET the bulk of each mission (the base you build, the army you mass, the map you fight on). The thing that persists must be a HOOK ("my stuff carried over"), never a SPREADSHEET. Concretely for THEATER: persist (1) a single named Hero/Commander unit that levels via the engine's existing GainsExperience trait, (2) a small Veteran Cadre of 3-6 units you choose to extract at mission end (XCOM roster + Homeworld fleet emotion), (3) a Nation Dossier of 3-5 binary/tiered identity perks you unlock by how you played (the "civ" layer, expressed as engine conditions/tech-unlocks, not buildings to micromanage), and (4) a developed Home Theater region rendered as a between-missions map you can spend a small Reconstruction budget on. RESET every mission: ore, cash, the tactical base/Construction Yard, the bulk army, and map control. The civ layer surfaces as a 30-60 second "Theater Map" interstitial with at most 3 clickable decisions, never a 4X screen. Anti-snowball is handled by per-mission economy reset (your big bank doesn't carry), diminishing perk returns, scaling mission difficulty, and a cadre cap; the death-spiral is handled by floors (heroes are downed not dead, you always get a minimum starting force, and a lost mission costs progress not the run). This reuses existing engine traits almost entirely — it is mod-data plus small C# for the meta-layer serialization, not an engine rewrite.
keyFindings: THE UNIVERSAL PATTERN: every successful campaign persists a SMALL, NAMED, EMOTIONAL set and resets the bulk. Homeworld dev: 'the ships were considered the characters' — persistence works because you feel attachment, not because you're managing a balance sheet. The danger zone (Civ/Stellaris) is exactly when the persistent thing becomes a large spreadsheet that scales tedium with size. THEATER must persist things you can NAME, not things you have to AUDIT.

DARK CRUSADE IS THE CLOSEST MODEL and the one to copy hardest: a meta-map of capturable provinces, a persistent leveling Commander with Wargear, and per-province Honor Guard units that accumulate into your army. Critically, Dark Crusade PERSISTED base structures per-province (snowball risk) while Soulstorm RESET them (you rebuild every battle). The user already rejected control-point-only economies, so THEATER should take Dark Crusade's persistent HERO + ROSTER + IDENTITY but Soulstorm's RESET-THE-BASE rule — you always rebuild your tactical base from a Construction Yard each mission. That single choice protects the sacred RA harvester/base-building loop AND kills the snowball.

DARK CRUSADE'S ANTI-SNOWBALL TRICK IS DIRECTLY REUSABLE: enemy strength scaled off a counter that rises over campaign TIME / their stronghold, NOT off how much territory they'd lost — so wiping the enemy off the map didn't make the remaining missions trivially easy; the final stronghold defenses stayed hard. THEATER's mission difficulty should scale with campaign PROGRESS (mission index / acts cleared), not with how strong the player's nation is, so a strong nation meets a proportionally harder mission — the challenge curve stays flat-ish regardless of snowball.

XCOM + WARCRAFT 3 + HOMEWORLD ALL CONVERGE ON 'PERSIST THE PEOPLE/SHIPS, RESET THE ECONOMY': XCOM persists the soldier roster (named, leveled, permadeath stakes) and the base, but each mission's tactical map and loadout-economy is fresh. WC3 persists hero level + items WITHIN an act but resets resources/base every mission, and explicitly RESETS hero gear at major act/faction boundaries (Arthas loses his items Human->Undead) to re-floor power. Homeworld persists the literal fleet and resources — the most emotionally powerful version — but is also the cautionary tale: it can hard-lock a player into an unrecoverable death spiral if an early fleet is gutted. THEATER wants XCOM/WC3's roster+hero persistence with Homeworld's emotion but must add the floors Homeworld lacked.

THE ECONOMY MUST RESET EACH MISSION — this is both the anti-snowball lynchpin AND the thing that protects the corrected hybrid thesis. If cash/ore stockpiles persisted, a rich nation would steamroll. Because every mission you start near-broke and must re-run the harvester loop + re-capture territory to fund yourself, the sacred RA economic tension (EXPAND-PROTECT-FIGHT triangle) is re-fought every single mission. Persistence lives in CAPABILITY (who you are, what you've unlocked, who survived), never in CAPITAL (how much money you banked). This is the single most important rule.

THE 'CIV LAYER' SHOULD BE EXPRESSED AS UNLOCKED IDENTITY PERKS (engine conditions / tech-unlocks), NOT AS DEVELOPED BUILDINGS YOU MANAGE. 'You develop the territory' becomes 'your Nation Dossier gains traits' — e.g. unlock a faction-wide passive (harvesters +1 armor), a new buildable unit, a support-power discount, a starting-loadout perk. These map 1:1 onto OpenRA's existing condition/prerequisite/Buildable system and require zero per-mission management. This is 'develop-the-ground as identity', the map-anchored civ verb the user wants, minus the menu tax.

ENGINE SUBSTRATE ALREADY EXISTS — this is mostly mod-data + a thin meta-serializer, not an engine rewrite: GainsExperience/GivesExperience/ProducibleWithLevel (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/) already implement unit veterancy = the Total War mechanic, perfect for the persistent Hero and Veteran Cadre. Capturable/CaptureManager/Captures + GivesCashOnCapture + the user's own Phase-0 SupplyNetwork/SupplyNode give the heterogeneous capturable-structure layer. TransformOnCapture, Production, and the condition/prerequisite system give the perk/tech layer. The ONLY genuinely new C# is: serialize a small CampaignState (hero level+wargear, cadre roster, dossier perks, theater-region state, mission index) to disk between missions, and inject it as actor inits / granted conditions at the next mission's start.

THE CONFIRMED LOBBY-TOGGLE PATTERN (crates/bounty checkboxes) tells you exactly how the MATCH-mode light civ layer should ship — a single non-persistent toggle — and by contrast tells you the CAMPAIGN layer is where persistence lives. Keep them architecturally identical (same perk/condition system) but differ only in whether CampaignState is written to disk. That means the civ system is built ONCE and reused across both modes.
recommendations: PERSIST A SINGLE NAMED HERO/COMMANDER (the WC3 + Dark Crusade hook). One unique unit that carries level, a few unlocked 'Wargear' slots (ability/stat modifiers), and a name across every mission. Implement with the existing GainsExperience trait + a small set of granted conditions for wargear. It is the primary emotional anchor and the cheapest to build. CRITICAL FLOOR: the hero is DOWNED, never permanently dead, on mission loss — it revives at the next mission minus one Wargear charge or at reduced level, so losing a mission stings without ending the run. This single unit does 80% of the 'my stuff carried over' emotional work for ~5% of the engineering.

PERSIST A SMALL VETERAN CADRE (XCOM roster + Homeworld fleet emotion), HARD-CAPPED at 4-6 units. At mission end, the player picks which SURVIVING units to 'extract' into the cadre (the Honor-Guard accumulation from Dark Crusade/Soulstorm). Next mission they arrive as pre-veteran reinforcements via the existing ProductionParadrop/ProductionFromMapEdge + ProducibleWithLevel traits. The CAP is the anti-snowball governor — you can never accumulate an unstoppable persistent army, you bring a hand-picked spearhead and must still build the bulk fresh each mission. Units that die in a mission are gone (XCOM permadeath stakes) but only cadre units — your mass army is expendable as always.

PERSIST A NATION DOSSIER OF 3-5 IDENTITY PERKS as the 'civ' layer — unlocked by HOW you played the prior mission (capture all derricks -> 'Industrialist' perk; finish under time -> 'Blitz' perk; protect all harvesters -> 'Logistics Corps' perk). Each perk is a single engine condition or Buildable-prerequisite granted at mission start: a faction-wide passive, a new unit unlocked, a cheaper support power. This is develop-the-ground-as-identity with ZERO per-mission management — you don't build or maintain anything, you just ARE a nation that fights a certain way now. Use DIMINISHING design: later perks are sidegrades/flavor, not raw power, so a fully-developed nation isn't strictly stronger, just more characterful (anti-snowball + dodges the 'optimal build' tax).

PERSIST A DEVELOPED HOME THEATER REGION as a tiny between-missions map (the Dark Crusade meta-map, shrunk to 'Foothold not Empire'). It shows 5-10 nodes you've liberated. Give a SMALL Reconstruction budget (earned from mission performance, NOT carried cash) to spend on at most ONE upgrade per interstitial — e.g. fortify a node (it starts pre-captured next mission), or convert a node's payoff type (resource <-> power). HARD CONSTRAINT: this screen presents AT MOST 3 choices and resolves in under 60 seconds. It is a decision, not a city-builder. If it ever needs scrollbars or tooltips-on-tooltips, it has failed the 'no management tax' test and must be cut back.

RESET EVERYTHING ELSE EVERY MISSION, explicitly and on purpose: cash/ore stockpile (always start near-broke), the tactical base and Construction Yard (always rebuild from scratch — this is the Soulstorm rule that protects the sacred RA loop), the bulk army, and map/territory control on the mission map itself. State this as a design law: PERSISTENCE = CAPABILITY (hero, cadre, dossier, home-region perks), RESET = CAPITAL (money, base, mass army, mission-map control). Re-running the harvester + territory economy from near-zero every mission is what keeps the EXPAND/PROTECT/FIGHT triangle alive and the pace twitchy.

SURFACE THE META AS A 30-60s INTERSTITIAL, NEVER A 4X SCREEN. Sequence: mission-end results -> 'extract your cadre' pick (one screen, click survivors) -> 'dossier unlock' reveal (automatic, a card flips, maybe one A/B choice) -> 'Theater Map' with at most one Reconstruction spend -> next mission briefing. Three clicks, no spreadsheets, no pause-to-think analysis paralysis. Borrow XCOM's between-mission RHYTHM (results -> roster -> next) but compress it. Everything is shown on a stylized map (map-anchored, the user's explicit want), never a menu of stats.

BUILD ANTI-SNOWBALL IN FROM DAY ONE WITH FOUR LAYERS (per the anti-snowball research + Dark Crusade's scaling trick): (1) economy resets each mission so no capital snowball; (2) cadre cap + diminishing-returns perks so capability can't run away; (3) mission difficulty scales with campaign PROGRESS not player strength (Dark Crusade's stronghold-defense stays hard regardless of how much map you hold) — a strong nation just meets a harder mission; (4) AVOID explicit rubber-banding — the research is clear that players hate visible catch-up. Keep it subtle: scale the enemy's starting forces and objectives, don't nerf the player's persistent stuff.

BUILD ANTI-DEATH-SPIRAL FLOORS so a lost mission costs PROGRESS, not the RUN (the explicit Homeworld failure to avoid): heroes are downed-not-dead; you ALWAYS get a guaranteed minimum starting force and base regardless of how badly the last mission went; a lost mission can be RETRIED or routed-around (Dark Crusade let you attack a different province) rather than hard-failing the campaign; and consider letting a defeat still grant a partial dossier/Reconstruction consolation so the player moves forward weakened but not stuck. Never let the persistent state drop below a floor where the next mission is unwinnable — that is the one thing Homeworld got wrong and the one trap the user named.

BUILD THE CIV SYSTEM ONCE, SHARE IT ACROSS MODES. The MATCH-mode light civ layer (toggleable, non-persistent) and the CAMPAIGN heavy civ layer use the SAME perk/condition/dossier machinery; the ONLY difference is whether CampaignState is serialized to disk between sessions. In MATCH, the dossier builds up during one match and dies at match end (the confirmed non-persistent rule). In CAMPAIGN, it's written to disk and reloaded. This keeps engineering minimal and guarantees the two modes feel like the same game.

PROTOTYPE PATH (cheap, reuses Phase-0 work): start with ONLY the persistent Hero (one GainsExperience unit serialized across two stitched-together skirmish missions) + a 3-perk dossier. Validate the single question the user cares about: does 'my commander leveled up and my nation became Industrialist' feel like meaningful development WITHOUT feeling like homework? If that hooks with zero new art (reskin an existing hero unit, e.g. Tanya/a named MCV), add the cadre, then the Theater-map Reconstruction screen. Do NOT build the full meta-map first — that's the part most likely to drift into the 4X tax the user is allergic to.
risks: THE THEATER-MAP RECONSTRUCTION SCREEN IS THE #1 DRIFT RISK toward the exact 4X management tax the user rejected. Every feature added to it (more nodes, more upgrade types, resource conversion chains, build queues) pushes it from 'a decision' toward 'a spreadsheet'. Mitigation: hard-cap it at 3 choices / 60 seconds forever, and treat any request for scrollbars/sub-menus as a red flag to cut, not expand. If in doubt, make the meta-layer THINNER.

SNOWBALL VIA PERSISTENT POWER PERKS: if dossier perks are raw power (+damage, +HP) rather than sidegrades/identity, a well-played early campaign compounds into trivial late missions. Mitigation: make perks characterful sidegrades and flavor (unlock a unit, change a payoff type, discount a power) rather than flat stat boosts, apply diminishing returns, and scale mission difficulty with campaign progress so the curve stays flat. This is the Dark Crusade lesson the user must not lose.

DEATH SPIRAL VIA PERSISTENT-LOSS COMPOUNDING (the Homeworld trap the user explicitly named): if losing a mission permanently guts the hero/cadre and the next mission assumes that strength, the player can reach an unwinnable state and the run is dead. Mitigation: heroes downed-not-dead, guaranteed minimum starting force/base, retry-or-route-around on loss, and a floor below which persistent state cannot drop. Losing must cost progress, never the run.

PERMADEATH STAKES VS FRUSTRATION TENSION: XCOM's emotional power comes from cadre units that can die forever — but that same permadeath, applied to a hero or to too much of your force, becomes a save-scumming or rage-quit driver in an RTS where unit loss is chaotic and less controllable than in turn-based XCOM. Mitigation: permadeath stakes apply ONLY to the optional cadre (and even then capped/small), never the hero, and never the expendable mass army. Make extraction (saving units) an active reward, not loss an active punishment.

PROTECTING THE SACRED RA LOOP: any persistence that lets the player skip re-building a base or re-running the harvester economy (e.g. persistent base structures a la Dark Crusade, or carried-over cash) directly erodes what makes RA fun and what the user is trying to preserve. Mitigation: enforce the CAPABILITY-persists / CAPITAL-resets law religiously; the base and economy are rebuilt from near-zero every single mission, no exceptions. The persistent layer sits ABOVE the RA loop, never inside it.

ENGINEERING SCOPE CREEP ON SERIALIZATION/DETERMINISM: the meta-layer writes state to disk and re-injects it as actor inits + granted conditions. This is outside world.Tick() so determinism rules don't bite, BUT if cadre/hero state is ever read inside the sim in a non-deterministic order it could desync in multiplayer-coop campaigns. Mitigation: keep CampaignState load as pre-game actor inits / Ruleset modifications only (the same path mods already use), never as runtime mutation of synced state; single-player campaign is the safe initial target.

OVER-PERSISTING (the spreadsheet creep): the temptation will be to persist 'just one more thing' (per-unit kill counts, named subordinate officers, regional happiness, tech trees with 20 nodes). Each addition individually seems small but collectively rebuilds the Stellaris tax. Mitigation: cap the persistent set at the four named pillars (Hero, Cadre, Dossier of <=5 perks, Home Region of <=10 nodes). If something new wants to persist, it must REPLACE a pillar, not add to the count.

precedents.name: Dawn of War: Dark Crusade
precedents.whatTheyDid: Meta-map of capturable provinces; a persistent leveling Commander with purchasable Wargear; per-province Honor Guard units that accumulate into your army across the campaign. Base STRUCTURES persisted per-province (you could fortify provinces with Listening Posts that were still there if attacked later).
precedents.outcome: Beloved as the gold-standard 'persistent faction conquers a map' campaign. The persistent Commander + accumulating Honor Guard were the emotional core. The persistent base structures were the snowball weak point (holding the map made you progressively dominant).
precedents.lessonForUs: Copy the persistent HERO + accumulating ROSTER + meta-map of capturable structures (THEATER's heterogeneous-payoff nodes fit perfectly). Take its anti-snowball trick: enemy strength scaled off campaign-time/stronghold, NOT off territory lost, so the final stronghold defense stayed hard regardless of your dominance. But do NOT persist tactical base structures.

precedents.name: Dawn of War: Soulstorm
precedents.whatTheyDid: Same meta-map as Dark Crusade but REMOVED persistent base structures — every battle you rebuild your base from scratch (with a narrow exception for Sisters of Battle forward bases). Honor Guard still accumulated.
precedents.outcome: Reduced the snowball relative to Dark Crusade; each battle re-engaged the core base-building loop. Generally seen as the more balanced (if less polished) of the two on this axis.
precedents.lessonForUs: This is THE rule that protects RA's sacred loop: persist the hero and roster, but RESET the base every mission. Adopt Soulstorm's reset-the-base over Dark Crusade's persist-the-base. It re-runs the harvester/base economy every mission, keeping the EXPAND/PROTECT/FIGHT triangle alive and killing the capital snowball.

precedents.name: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
precedents.whatTheyDid: Persists a soldier ROSTER (named, class-leveled, permadeath) and a single persistent BASE across missions; each mission is a fresh tactical map with no carried battlefield economy. Memorial Wall commemorates dead soldiers.
precedents.outcome: The persistent named roster with permadeath stakes is one of the most emotionally sticky meta-systems in strategy gaming — 'your stuff carries over' plus 'you can lose them forever' creates attachment and tension.
precedents.lessonForUs: Persist a small Veteran Cadre with names and the option to extract survivors (attachment) and real but capped permadeath stakes (tension). Borrow the between-mission RHYTHM (results -> roster -> deploy) but compress it to seconds. Diversify the cadre so one loss isn't catastrophic — XCOM explicitly warns against over-investing in a few vets.

precedents.name: Warcraft 3 Campaign
precedents.whatTheyDid: Persists hero LEVEL + ITEMS within a campaign act; resources/base reset every mission. Deliberately RESETS hero gear at major boundaries (Arthas loses inventory transitioning Human->Undead).
precedents.outcome: The leveling persistent hero is the campaign's spine and a huge attachment driver; the periodic gear reset re-floors power so later acts aren't trivialized and stay tense.
precedents.lessonForUs: Make the persistent Hero the campaign's spine (cheapest, highest emotional ROI). Use act/chapter boundaries as deliberate RE-FLOOR points (strip some Wargear, reset to a baseline) to prevent snowball and keep the difficulty curve honest — persistence within an act, partial reset between acts.

precedents.name: Homeworld
precedents.whatTheyDid: Persists the literal FLEET and resources mission-to-mission — the ships you end with are the ships you start with. Devs treated 'the ships as the characters'.
precedents.outcome: The most emotionally powerful persistence in the genre (not resetting your fleet creates genuine attachment and stakes), BUT also the clearest death-spiral cautionary tale: a player who loses key ships early with limited resources can reach an unrecoverable state.
precedents.lessonForUs: Chase Homeworld's EMOTION (a force you grew and don't want to lose) but explicitly fix its flaw: never let persistent losses compound into an unwinnable state. Add the floors Homeworld lacked — guaranteed minimum starting force, downed-not-dead heroes, retry/route-around on loss. Capping the persistent cadre (vs Homeworld's whole fleet) is the key safety valve.

precedents.name: Star Wars: Empire at War — Galactic Conquest
precedents.whatTheyDid: Galactic strategic layer: surviving units, conquered planets, built defenses, and tech-gated heroes all persist; heroes die permanently; the galaxy state evolves with wins/losses. Tech tier unlocks new heroes/units.
precedents.outcome: Created an evolving strategic landscape feeding tactical battles, but the strategic layer carries real management overhead (economy, garrisons, infrastructure across many planets) — closer to the 4X tax the user wants to avoid as it scales.
precedents.lessonForUs: Cautionary scale lesson: the galactic layer is engaging but its management cost scales with empire size — exactly the tedium the user rejects. THEATER's 'Foothold not Empire' framing is the corrective: keep the meta-map to ~5-10 nodes in ONE theater, not a galaxy, so the strategic layer never grows into a spreadsheet. Persist tech-gated UNIT UNLOCKS (good, low-management) but not sprawling planet-by-planet infrastructure.

precedents.name: Total War Campaign
precedents.whatTheyDid: Campaign map persists provinces, armies, and per-unit VETERANCY/experience (units rank up by fighting); generals/lords gain levels and skills. Replenishing casualties with green troops DILUTES a unit's experience.
precedents.outcome: Veterancy creates deep attachment to specific units, but the full campaign map is a heavy 4X management layer with significant analysis-paralysis surface.
precedents.lessonForUs: Steal the UNIT-VETERANCY mechanic (already in OpenRA as GainsExperience/ProducibleWithLevel) for the persistent hero and cadre — and steal the casualty-dilution idea as a subtle anti-snowball governor (rebuilt cadre units come back at reduced veterancy). But REJECT the full campaign-map management surface — that's the analysis-paralysis the user explicitly wants to avoid.

campaign-meta.detail:
CAMPAIGN META-PROGRESSION DESIGN FOR THEATER — full specification.

== THE ONE LAW ==
PERSISTENCE = CAPABILITY. RESET = CAPITAL.
Persist who you ARE and who SURVIVED. Reset what you OWN. Every successful precedent obeys some version of this; every failure (Homeworld death-spiral, Stellaris tedium, Dark Crusade snowball) is a violation of it. This single law resolves almost every design question below.

== THE FOUR PERSISTENT PILLARS (and nothing else) ==
Cap the persistent set at exactly four things you can NAME, never AUDIT:

1) THE COMMANDER (Hero) — one unique named unit. Persists: level (via existing GainsExperience trait), a small set of unlocked Wargear (each = a granted engine condition/ability). Emotional spine of the campaign (WC3/Dark Crusade). Downed-not-dead on loss. Highest emotional ROI per unit of engineering — build this FIRST. Reskin an existing hero (Tanya, a named MCV/MCV-hero) for zero new art.

2) THE VETERAN CADRE — 3-6 units, HARD-CAPPED. At mission end you pick which SURVIVORS to extract (Honor Guard accumulation, XCOM roster, Homeworld emotion). They return next mission as pre-veteran reinforcements (ProductionParadrop/ProductionFromMapEdge + ProducibleWithLevel). Cadre units can die permanently (XCOM stakes); your mass army cannot persist and is expendable as always. The CAP is the anti-snowball governor.

3) THE NATION DOSSIER — 3-5 identity perks, the 'civ' layer. Each = one engine condition or Buildable prerequisite granted at mission start. Unlocked by HOW you play (capture all derricks -> Industrialist; protect all harvesters -> Logistics Corps; finish fast -> Blitz). Perks are CHARACTERFUL SIDEGRADES (unlock a unit, change a node's payoff type, discount a power), NOT flat power — diminishing returns by design. This is 'develop-the-ground-as-identity' with zero per-mission management: you don't build or maintain anything, you simply ARE a nation that fights a certain way now.

4) THE HOME THEATER — a tiny meta-map of 5-10 liberated nodes ('Foothold not Empire'). A small Reconstruction budget (earned from mission performance, NOT carried cash) buys at most ONE upgrade per interstitial: fortify a node (starts pre-captured next mission) or convert its payoff type (resource <-> power/vision/production). At most 3 choices, under 60 seconds. A decision, not a city-builder.

== WHAT RESETS EVERY MISSION (on purpose) ==
- Cash/ore stockpile — always start near-broke. (THE anti-snowball lynchpin.)
- The tactical base + Construction Yard — always rebuild from scratch (Soulstorm rule; protects the sacred RA loop).
- The bulk army — expendable, never persists.
- Map/territory control on the mission map — re-fought each time.
Re-running the harvester + territory economy from near-zero every mission is what keeps the corrected HYBRID thesis (EXPAND richer ore <-> PROTECT harvesters <-> FIGHT for map control) alive and twitchy in EVERY mission, not just the first.

== THE BETWEEN-MISSIONS FLOW (30-60s, three clicks, map-anchored) ==
Mission results -> [click] extract cadre survivors -> [auto/card-flip, maybe one A/B] dossier unlock reveal -> [Theater Map, at most one Reconstruction spend] -> next briefing. Everything on a stylized map, never a stats menu. Borrow XCOM's results->roster->deploy rhythm, compressed. If it ever needs scrollbars or nested tooltips, it has failed the no-management-tax test — cut it back.

== ANTI-SNOWBALL (four layers, per the research + Dark Crusade) ==
1) Economy resets each mission — no capital snowball.
2) Cadre cap + diminishing-returns/sidegrade perks — capability can't run away.
3) Mission difficulty scales with campaign PROGRESS (mission index / acts cleared), NOT player strength — Dark Crusade's stronghold-defense stayed hard regardless of dominance. A strong nation just meets a harder mission; the curve stays flat-ish.
4) NO visible rubber-banding — the anti-snowball research is explicit that players hate it. Scale enemy starting forces/objectives subtly; never nerf the player's persistent stuff. Optional Total-War-style governor: rebuilt cadre units return at reduced veterancy (casualty dilution).
Use act/chapter boundaries as deliberate RE-FLOOR points (WC3 Arthas gear reset): strip some Wargear / reset to a baseline so late acts aren't trivial.

== ANTI-DEATH-SPIRAL (the Homeworld trap the user named) ==
- Hero is DOWNED, not dead — revives next mission at reduced level / minus one Wargear charge.
- GUARANTEED minimum starting force + base every mission regardless of last mission's outcome.
- A lost mission can be RETRIED or ROUTED AROUND (Dark Crusade let you hit a different province) — never a hard campaign-fail.
- Optionally a defeat still grants partial dossier/Reconstruction consolation: move forward weakened, not stuck.
- A FLOOR below which persistent state cannot drop, so the next mission is always winnable. Losing costs PROGRESS, never the RUN.

== ENGINE REUSE (mostly mod-data + a thin meta-serializer) ==
Already present in OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/: GainsExperience / GivesExperience / ProducibleWithLevel (unit veterancy = the hero & cadre); Capturable / CaptureManager / Captures / GivesCashOnCapture (heterogeneous capturable nodes); TransformOnCapture, Production, and the condition/prerequisite/Buildable system (the perk & tech layer). Plus the user's own Phase-0 SupplyNetwork/SupplyNode for connected-territory payoff.
The ONLY genuinely new C#: serialize a small CampaignState (hero level+wargear, cadre roster, dossier perks, theater-region node state, mission index) to disk between missions, and re-inject it at the next mission's start as PRE-GAME actor inits + Ruleset/condition modifications (the same path mods already use) — NOT runtime mutation of synced state, so determinism rules don't bite. Target single-player campaign first; coop multiplayer needs care that CampaignState is loaded identically on all clients pre-game.

== SHARED WITH MATCH MODE ==
The MATCH light-civ layer (toggleable, non-persistent — like the crates/bounty checkboxes) and the CAMPAIGN heavy-civ layer use the SAME perk/condition/dossier machinery. The only difference: whether CampaignState is written to disk. In MATCH the dossier builds during one match and dies at match end. Build the system ONCE; both modes feel like the same game.

== PROTOTYPE PATH (cheap, validates the one question) ==
Start with ONLY the persistent Commander (one GainsExperience unit serialized across two stitched skirmish missions) + a 3-perk dossier. Reskin an existing hero — zero new art. Validate: does 'my commander leveled and my nation became Industrialist' feel like meaningful DEVELOPMENT without feeling like HOMEWORK? If it hooks, add the cadre, then the Theater-map Reconstruction screen. Do NOT build the full meta-map first — that's the piece most likely to drift into the 4X tax the user is allergic to.

Relevant files in the repo: /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/design/PHASE0-README.md (the rejected replacement-thesis prototype and the existing SupplyNetwork/SupplyNode work to reuse), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/ (GainsExperience.cs, ProducibleWithLevel.cs, Capturable.cs, CaptureManager.cs, GivesCashOnCapture.cs, TransformOnCapture.cs, Production.cs — the reusable substrate), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/design/game-design-vision.md and contemporary-openra-design.md (existing design vocabulary to align with).

match-light.executiveSummary: Design the MATCHES civ layer as ONE legible verb on top of structures that are always on. The capturable territory-structures (some give resources, some give powers) are just Red Alert tech buildings and should ALWAYS be present and capturable regardless of the toggle — they don't fork balance because capturing a tech building is already core RA. The toggle gates only the thin "develop the ground" layer on top: the ability to invest in a structure you hold to upgrade it ONE tier, governed by a single map-anchored "Foothold" meter and a one-time Doctrine identity pick. "Off" = territory plays exactly like RA tech buildings (capture, get the static reward). "On" = held structures can be developed one tier and you make one Doctrine choice; the map, not a menu, is where you see and act on all of it. The single hardest constraint is psychological: if the optimal player MUST micromanage the civ layer, it is not optional — so every develop action must be a LOW-FREQUENCY, set-and-forget commitment (seconds of attention per several minutes), never a per-unit or per-tick chore, and its payoff must be roughly attention-neutral vs. ignoring it (a different identity, not a strictly higher ceiling). Precedents say this works when the optional layer is map-anchored background state that resolves between fights (Rise of Nations, Company of Heroes territory, WC3 neutral buildings) and forks the community when the toggle changes the WINNING actions rather than the flavor (Fortnite no-build, format-balance splits). Recommendation: ship territory-structures always-on; gate Foothold+Doctrine+upgrade-tier behind a single lobby checkbox (default ON in unranked, locked OFF for ranked 1v1); cap the whole layer at ~3-4 discrete decisions per match; cut all per-unit development, tech trees, and persistence to campaign.
keyFindings: SEPARATE THE TWO THINGS THE TOGGLE COULD CONTROL. There are two distinct layers being conflated: (a) the heterogeneous capturable territory-structures themselves, and (b) the 'civ development' on top of them. (a) should ALWAYS be on — a capturable structure that gives income or a power is literally an RA tech building (Oil Derrick, Hospital, Radar Dome already exist), and OpenRA players already expect to fight over them. Only (b) — the ability to DEVELOP a structure you hold — should be the toggle. This is the cleanest answer to 'does the toggle fork balance into two games': it doesn't, because the map layout, the structures, and the capture game are identical in both modes. Only an additive investment verb appears/disappears.

THE MINIMAL 'DEVELOP THE GROUND' VERB SET FOR A MATCH IS THREE THINGS, NOT A SYSTEM.
