(1) UPGRADE-ONE-TIER: a structure you currently hold can be invested in once to reach a single better tier (richer income, longer-range vision, faster power charge) — implemented as the existing Transforms/upgrade pattern, one click, a build-time delay, done. No tier 2/3 ladder in a match. (2) A SINGLE 'FOOTHOLD' METER: one legible 0-100 bar fed passively by how much developed territory you hold, that crosses at most TWO thresholds during a 40-min match, each unlocking a small global capability (e.g. at 50% your developed structures auto-repair; at 100% one extra build queue or a faction power). One meter, two ledger entries, visible on the map not in a panel. (3) ONE DOCTRINE PICK: a single irreversible identity fork made once, early (Economic / Military / Civic-Support), that recolors what developing means for you — not a tech tree. That is the entire civ layer for a match.

MAP-ANCHORING IS THE LOAD-BEARING ANTI-BLOAT MECHANISM, NOT A NICE-TO-HAVE. Every develop action must be performed BY clicking the structure on the battlefield and must be SEEN as a change to that structure's sprite/banner on the battlefield. No second resource panel, no city screen, no build menu for the civ layer. This is the Company-of-Heroes / Rise-of-Nations lesson: the strategic layer stays fast precisely because it is the same map you are already fighting on, read with your eyes during a fight, not a spreadsheet you pause to open. It also keeps eyes ON the battlefield by definition — the civ layer has no off-map UI to pull the camera away.

THE PSYCHOLOGY: 'OPTIONAL' DIES THE MOMENT THE OPTIMAL PLAYER MUST MICRO IT. The failure mode is not UI clutter, it is APM tax. If developing territory is a strictly-higher-ceiling action that the best player spams every time it's available, then it is mandatory APM dressed as a choice, and casual players who ignore it just lose. The fix is twofold: (i) FREQUENCY — each develop action is a one-time, set-and-forget commitment measured in seconds-of-attention per several-minutes, never a per-tick or per-unit recurring chore (the thing the user already rejected about harvester-replacement was meaninglessness; the thing to avoid here is busywork); (ii) PAYOFF SHAPE — developing should buy a DIFFERENT identity (sidegrade) more than a bigger number, so that a player who never touches the civ layer and just plays clean RA is still competitive. Aim for 'attention-neutral': the time you spend developing is time you didn't spend macroing your army, and the two should trade roughly evenly.

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE KEEPS IT INSIDE THE FLOW CHANNEL. Minute one must be pure Red Alert — harvest, build, fight. The develop verb should not even be offerable until the player has captured their first territory-structure (just-in-time: the first capture pops a single one-line prompt 'Hold this and you can develop it', then never nags again). The Doctrine pick should surface only when the Foothold meter first ticks up, not at match start as a 4X-style pre-game system dump. This mirrors the validated Codex/just-in-time-tutor approach already in the project's design doc: the layer reveals itself in the moment it becomes relevant, so newcomers never face a system they don't yet need.

TOGGLE DEFAULTS AND LOCKING DECIDE WHETHER THE COMMUNITY FORKS. The lesson from competitive RTS format-balance and from Fortnite's no-build split is that a toggle forks the community when the two states reward DIFFERENT winning actions and BOTH have serious ladders. Mitigation: (1) keep ONE canonical competitive mode (ranked 1v1 has the civ layer LOCKED OFF, like the project doc already plans for diplomacy) so there is a single thing to balance around; (2) make the develop layer ADDITIVE and identity-flavored rather than a separate meta, so 'on' is 'RA-plus-a-bit' not 'a different game'; (3) default ON in unranked/co-op/comp-stomp where depth-seekers live, default/locked OFF in ranked. This gives the depth-seeking audience their layer without splitting the balance burden or the ladder.

CUT LIST (MATCH-ONLY -> PUSH TO CAMPAIGN): multi-tier upgrade ladders (tier 2/3/4 in one match), any tech TREE for the civ layer, per-unit/per-squad development or veterancy-as-civ, population/food management beyond a single soft meter, anything PERSISTENT (a developed structure must die at match end — non-persistence is a stated decision), inter-structure adjacency/synergy puzzles (analysis paralysis), and any develop action that recurs on a timer. All of these are exactly the 'tedium that scales with size / pause-to-think / analysis paralysis' the user wants kept out of MATCHES — they belong to the heavier, persistent CAMPAIGN lean.

THE ENGINE ALREADY HAS EVERY PIECE — THIS IS MOD-DATA + SMALL C#, NOT A REWRITE. Verified in repo: LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox.cs) is literally the crates/bounty checkbox pattern and grants tech-tree prerequisites when ticked — that IS the toggle. Transforms/TransformOnCapture give the 'upgrade one tier' verb. The Capturable/Captures/GivesCashOnCapture family + ProvidesPrerequisite give the always-on territory-structures. GrantConditionOnPrerequisite + GrantConditionOnPlayerResources + the GrantCondition* family wire the Foothold thresholds to global capabilities. ScriptLobbyDropdown handles the Doctrine pick. The Foothold meter is the one genuinely new bit (a small world-trait counter, same shape as the existing SupplyNetwork prototype trait), and it stays deterministic with integer-only math.
recommendations: SHIP THE STRUCTURES ALWAYS-ON, TOGGLE ONLY THE DEVELOP LAYER. Place the heterogeneous capturable structures (resource-givers AND power-givers) on every map unconditionally — they are RA tech buildings (reuse Capturable + GivesCashOnCapture/ProvidesPrerequisite). Add ONE lobby checkbox 'Develop Territory' (via LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox, mirroring Crates/Bounty). When OFF: capture gives the static reward, full stop — pure RA. When ON: a held structure exposes a single 'Develop' command and the Foothold meter + Doctrine pick become active. The map, structures, and capture game are byte-identical in both states, so the toggle cannot fork balance.

DEFINE THE DEVELOP VERB AS EXACTLY ONE TIER, ONE CLICK, MAP-ANCHORED. Select a structure you currently own/hold -> 'Develop' (costs credits + a build-time delay, no new resource) -> it visibly upgrades its banner/sprite and steps up its single payoff (income node pays more / vision node sees farther / power node charges faster). Implement with the existing Transforms pattern. No tier 2. The cost competes with your army spend (the Sid Meier 'interesting choice' = develop the node OR build two more tanks, never both), which is what keeps it from being free mandatory value.

IMPLEMENT FOOTHOLD AS ONE METER WITH TWO THRESHOLDS, SHOWN ON THE MAP. A single 0-100 'Foothold' bar fed passively by the count/tier of developed structures you hold (integer math, recompute on a slow interval exactly like the existing SupplyNetwork trait — no per-tick float). It crosses at most two thresholds in a match, each granting ONE global passive capability via GrantConditionOnPrerequisite (e.g. 50%: developed structures self-repair; 100%: a faction support-power or one extra production slot). Render it as a thin bar near the existing power/cash readout AND reflect it on the structures themselves. No second economy panel.

MAKE DOCTRINE ONE IRREVERSIBLE PICK, SURFACED JUST-IN-TIME. When Foothold first ticks above zero, offer a one-time radial/dropdown (ScriptLobbyDropdown or a small in-world prompt): Economic (develop = more income), Military (develop = the Foothold powers are combat ones), or Civic-Support (develop = vision/repair/heal auras). One choice, locked for the match, recolors what developing means — an IDENTITY fork, not a tech tree. This is the CoH-doctrine lesson at minimal scope and is the main source of replay variety from the layer.

BUDGET THE WHOLE LAYER AT ~3-4 DISCRETE DECISIONS PER 40-MIN MATCH AND ENFORCE IT. Concretely: 1 Doctrine pick + ~2-3 Develop commitments across the match + reacting to 2 Foothold thresholds. That is the entire attention budget. Write it down as a balance invariant and lint/playtest against it: if a system encourages a 5th, 6th, 7th develop click per match, it has become APM and must be redesigned (e.g. raise the cost, add a per-match develop cap, or make later develops auto-trigger from Foothold rather than clicked).

GUARANTEE 'ATTENTION-NEUTRALITY' SO IGNORING THE LAYER IS VIABLE. Tune so that a player who never develops anything and just plays clean RA macro is competitive against a player who develops — the developer trades army-time for territory-payoff at roughly 1:1 value. Validate this directly in playtest: a 'develop-blind' player vs a 'develop-heavy' player of equal skill should win ~50/50, with different-feeling games. If develop-heavy wins >~60%, the layer is mandatory APM and the payoff must be flattened toward sidegrade.

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: GATE THE VERB BEHIND THE FIRST CAPTURE, GATE DOCTRINE BEHIND FIRST FOOTHOLD. Do not show any civ UI at match start. The first time the player captures a territory-structure, fire ONE just-in-time line ('Hold this — you can Develop it'), then stop. The Doctrine prompt appears only at first Foothold gain. This keeps minute-one as pure Red Alert and reveals the layer exactly when it becomes relevant (same just-in-time philosophy as the project's Codex).

RANKED 1v1 LOCKS THE TOGGLE OFF; UNRANKED/CO-OP DEFAULTS IT ON. Maintain one canonical competitive surface to balance around (civ layer locked off in ranked 1v1, exactly as the design doc already plans for diplomacy). Default the checkbox ON in skirmish-vs-AI, co-op, and comp-stomp where the depth-seeking audience plays, and offer it as a normal toggleable option in custom lobbies. This prevents the Fortnite/format-split failure: the depth lives where depth-seekers are, the ladder stays single and clean.

BUILD IT AS A PHASE-1 ZERO-NEW-ART SPIKE ON TOP OF THE EXISTING PROTOTYPE. Reuse Oil-Derrick/Radar/Hospital art for the three structure archetypes (income/vision/support), use a recolored banner or the existing upgrade-sprite swap for 'developed', and reuse the power-bar widget for Foothold. The only new C# is the Foothold world-trait (model it on design/.../SupplyNetwork.cs already in the repo) and a thin Develop order. Everything else is YAML wiring of LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox + Transforms + GrantConditionOnPrerequisite + Capturable. Kill-gate it the same way Phase 0 was gated: playtest for 'do my eyes stay on the battlefield, and is ignoring the layer still viable?'
risks: MANDATORY-APM CREEP IS THE PRIMARY RISK. Even a one-click develop verb becomes mandatory if its payoff outpaces its attention cost; the optimal player will then spam it and the 'optional' framing collapses. Mitigation: hard per-match develop cap, attention-neutral payoff tuning, and a balance invariant that develop-blind players win ~50%. This must be the #1 thing the playtest measures.

DOUBLE-WALLET REGRESSION. If Foothold or develop introduces a second spendable resource, you recreate the 'second wallet / control-point game' the user already rejected. Mitigation: develop is paid in CREDITS (one wallet), and Foothold is a STATE meter that is never spent, only crossed. Audit the design for any new spendable counter and reject it.

TOGGLE-FORKS-BALANCE if the develop layer changes winning actions rather than flavor. If 'on' rewards fundamentally different builds/timings than 'off' and both get serious ladders, the community and the balance team split (the format-balance and Fortnite-no-build lesson). Mitigation: additive + identity-flavored layer, single canonical ranked mode with it locked off, default-on only in non-ladder contexts.

MAP-AUTHORING BURDEN. Heterogeneous structures + Foothold thresholds need deliberate placement per map to be fair and symmetric; bad placement makes the layer feel arbitrary (the Phase-0 auto-placer already hit this). Mitigation: keep the auto-placer for skirmish but treat hand-placed structures as the quality bar; ensure mirror-symmetry on competitive maps.

DETERMINISM/DESYNC if Foothold is computed with float or wall-clock, or if the develop order isn't routed through the normal order pipeline. Mitigation: integer-only Foothold recompute on a fixed tick interval (copy the existing SupplyNetwork trait's approach), [Sync] the meter, and issue Develop as a standard IResolveOrder order — no UI state in sim.

LEGIBILITY OVERLOAD. Three structure archetypes x a Doctrine that recolors them x a meter could become hard to read at RA pace. Mitigation: strict visual language — one icon per archetype, the developed state is an obvious sprite/banner change, Foothold is a single bar; if a new player can't explain what a structure does at a glance, simplify before adding.

SCOPE BLEED FROM CAMPAIGN. The persistent, heavier campaign civ layer will tempt features back into MATCHES (tiers, trees, persistence). Mitigation: treat the cut-list as a hard wall; anything persistent or multi-tier is campaign-only by definition, and the match layer is frozen at Doctrine + one-tier-develop + one meter.

precedents.name: Company of Heroes — territory-as-economy with auto-resolving sectors
precedents.whatTheyDid: Resource income is tied directly to map sectors you hold; capturing/cutting territory IS the economy, and most of it resolves passively once a sector is captured rather than requiring constant micro. Veterancy and global upgrades add depth but are low-frequency commitments, not per-tick chores.
precedents.outcome: The canonical 'territory is the game' RTS; depth comes from the map you're already fighting on, not a separate panel. Already cited as the model in this project's own design doc.
precedents.lessonForUs: Map-anchor the civ layer and make holding/developing territory mostly passive-once-committed. This is the proof that 'develop the ground' can be deep without being a spreadsheet — copy the auto-resolving, map-read-with-your-eyes property.

precedents.name: Warcraft 3 — neutral buildings, mercenary camps, creep camps
precedents.whatTheyDid: Optional map-anchored power sources (taverns, goblin labs, mercenary camps, creeps with item/XP drops) that any player can contest. They're available only after a delay, are physically on the map, and reward map control with capability rather than just cash.
precedents.outcome: A celebrated layer of optional strategic depth that created tempo and map-control decisions without bloating the core macro — widely regarded as a high point of RTS map design.
precedents.lessonForUs: Exactly the template for heterogeneous capturable structures that give POWERS not just cash, gated by map control. Make them contestable and map-anchored; let the develop verb be the WC3 'go claim and use it' decision, not a menu.

precedents.name: StarCraft 2 Co-op Commanders & Mastery (vs 1v1 ladder)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Built a deep progression/mastery and commander-identity layer that lives ENTIRELY in co-op, completely separate from the 1v1 ladder which stays clean and canonical. Mastery choices are low-frequency identity picks (pick 1 of 2 perks), not per-game APM.
precedents.outcome: Co-op became hugely popular with the depth/PvE-seeking audience while 1v1 ladder balance was never touched by it. Two audiences served, ONE competitive surface to balance.
precedents.lessonForUs: This is the toggle-without-forking blueprint: put the heavier optional depth where the depth-seekers are (here: unranked/co-op, default-on) and keep ONE canonical ranked mode with the layer off. Identity-pick depth, not APM depth.

precedents.name: Rise of Nations — strategic systems as low-frequency background state
precedents.whatTheyDid: Layered Civ-style systems (territory borders, attrition, era advancement, tax/commerce caps) onto an RTS but kept the strategic decisions LOW-FREQUENCY and set between fights, so they never competed with moment-to-moment combat micro.
precedents.outcome: Successfully fused 4X depth with RTS pace; cited in this project's doc as the anti-Stellaris model precisely because depth came from a few cross-coupling systems set as background state, not many parallel meters.
precedents.lessonForUs: Keep Foothold/Doctrine as low-frequency background state crossed between fights, not decisions made DURING fights. Cap the on-screen choice density; the moment the civ layer demands attention mid-fight on the opponent's tempo, it has failed.

precedents.name: Fortnite — the no-build / build community split
precedents.whatTheyDid: Introduced a 'no-build' mode that removed the build mechanic. Because building was a core skill expression, no-build wasn't a flavor toggle — it was a fundamentally different game rewarding different actions, and it got its own full ranked ecosystem.
precedents.outcome: Genuinely split the community into two camps with two metas and two balance conversations; many players treated them as separate games.
precedents.lessonForUs: The cautionary tale. A toggle forks the community when it changes WINNING ACTIONS and both states get serious competition. Avoid by keeping the develop layer ADDITIVE/identity-flavored (RA-plus-a-bit) and by NOT giving the 'on' state its own ranked ladder — ranked stays single, with the layer off.

precedents.name: Competitive RTS format-balance (1v1 vs 2v2/team) split
precedents.whatTheyDid: RTS games that try to balance multiple formats (1v1, 2v2, 3v3) discover units/strategies that are fine in one format and broken in another; devs must pick ONE format to balance around (e.g. Stormgate chose 1v1 by design).
precedents.outcome: Repeatedly, teams that split balance attention across formats end up with a weaker primary mode and a fractured competitive community; the durable answer is to pick one canonical mode.
precedents.lessonForUs: Don't let the toggle create a second thing you must balance. Designate ranked 1v1 (civ layer OFF) as the single canonical competitive surface; the develop layer is explicitly a non-ladder, unranked-and-co-op enrichment, so balance attention never forks.

match-light.detail:
## The core move: separate the structures from the development

The brief asks whether the territory-structures should always be on while only the civ layer toggles. Yes — and this is the single most important decision. There are two layers being conflated:

- Layer A — the heterogeneous capturable structures (some give resources, some give powers/vision/repair/charge). These ARE Red Alert tech buildings. OpenRA already ships Oil Derrick (GivesCashOnCapture), Hospital, Radar Dome, Tech buildings that ProvidesPrerequisite. Players already expect to fight over them. They should ALWAYS be present and capturable, in both toggle states.
- Layer B — "develop the ground": investing in a structure you hold to make it better, plus a meter and an identity choice. This is the only thing the toggle controls.

Because Layer A is identical in both states (same map, same structures, same capture game), the toggle physically cannot fork balance at the level of map control. It only adds/removes an investment verb. That is the structural answer to "does a toggle fork balance into two games."

## What "off" vs "on" actually changes

- OFF: capture a structure -> get its static reward (income trickle, vision, a power). Pure Red Alert tech-building behavior. This is the canonical competitive state.
- ON: you ALSO get (1) a "Develop" command on structures you hold, (2) a single Foothold meter, (3) one Doctrine pick. Everything additive; nothing about the base game changes.

## The minimal develop-verb set (the whole match civ layer)

1. Upgrade-one-tier (the develop verb). Select a held structure -> Develop -> pay credits + build delay -> it visibly steps up its single payoff. One tier only, ever, in a match. Engine: Transforms / TransformOnCapture (both verified in repo). The cost competes with army spend, which is the Sid-Meier interesting-choice property and the main brake against it being free mandatory value.

2. One Foothold meter. A single 0–100 bar fed passively by how much developed territory you hold. Crosses at most two thresholds per 40-min match; each grants one global passive capability via GrantConditionOnPrerequisite (e.g. 50%: developed structures self-repair; 100%: a faction power or one extra build slot). It is STATE, never spent — no second wallet. Engine: a small world-trait counter modeled on the existing SupplyNetwork.cs prototype trait (integer-only, slow-interval recompute, [Sync]ed) — deterministic and lockstep-safe.

3. One Doctrine pick. A single irreversible identity fork (Economic / Military / Civic-Support), surfaced just-in-time when Foothold first ticks up. Recolors what "develop" means for you. Engine: ScriptLobbyDropdown or a small in-world prompt. This is the CoH-doctrine lesson at minimum scope and the main source of replay variety.

Total attention budget: ~1 Doctrine pick + ~2–3 Develop commitments + reacting to 2 Foothold thresholds = 3–4 discrete decisions across a whole match. Enforce this as a balance invariant.

## What to CUT to campaign-only

Multi-tier upgrade ladders (tier 2/3/4 in one match), any civ-layer tech TREE, per-unit/per-squad development or veterancy-as-civ, population/food beyond one soft meter, ANYTHING persistent (developed structures die at match end — a stated decision), adjacency/synergy puzzles (analysis paralysis), and any develop action that recurs on a timer. These are exactly the "tedium that scales with size / pause-to-think / analysis paralysis" the user wants out of MATCHES. They belong to the heavier, persistent CAMPAIGN.

## The psychology (the real constraint)

"Optional" dies the instant the optimal player MUST micro the layer. The failure isn't UI clutter — it's APM tax. Two guards:

- Frequency: every develop action is a one-time, set-and-forget commitment (seconds of attention per several minutes), never a per-tick or per-unit chore. A hard per-match develop cap backs this up.
- Payoff shape: developing buys a different IDENTITY (sidegrade) more than a bigger number. Target attention-neutrality — time spent developing is time not spent macroing the army, traded ~1:1. Validate directly: an equally-skilled develop-blind player should beat a develop-heavy player ~50% of the time, with different-feeling games. If develop-heavy wins >~60%, flatten the payoff toward sidegrade.

## Map-anchoring + progressive disclosure keep it in the flow channel

Every develop action is performed BY clicking the structure on the battlefield and SEEN as a change to that structure on the battlefield. No off-map panel, no city screen — so the civ layer has nothing that can pull the camera off the fight (Company of Heroes / Rise of Nations property). Disclosure: minute one is pure RA; the develop verb isn't offerable until the player's first capture (one just-in-time line, then silence); the Doctrine prompt appears only at first Foothold gain. Same just-in-time philosophy as the project's Codex.

## The toggle design and not-forking-the-community

Use LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox (verified — it's literally the Crates/Bounty checkbox pattern and grants tech-tree prerequisites when ticked). Defaults: ON in skirmish-vs-AI / co-op / comp-stomp (where depth-seekers live), a normal toggle in custom lobbies, LOCKED OFF in ranked 1v1. Keep ONE canonical competitive surface to balance around (same plan the design doc already has for diplomacy). The develop layer is additive and identity-flavored — "RA-plus-a-bit," not a separate meta — and it deliberately does NOT get its own ranked ladder. That is how SC2 co-op served the depth audience without ever touching 1v1 balance, and the inverse of the Fortnite no-build split (which forked because no-build changed winning actions AND got its own full competitive ecosystem).

## Build path (zero new art, mostly YAML + one small C# trait)

Reuse Oil-Derrick / Radar / Hospital art for the three archetypes (income / vision / support); developed state = recolored banner or the existing upgrade sprite-swap; Foothold = the existing power-bar widget. The only genuinely new C# is the Foothold world-trait (copy design/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/SupplyNetwork.cs's integer-only, interval-recompute shape) and a thin Develop order routed through the normal IResolveOrder pipeline. Everything else is YAML wiring of LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox + Transforms + GrantConditionOnPrerequisite + GrantConditionOnPlayerResources + Capturable/GivesCashOnCapture/ProvidesPrerequisite — all verified present in OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/. Kill-gate it like Phase 0: playtest two questions — do my eyes stay on the battlefield, and is ignoring the layer still viable?

## Relevant files in the repo (absolute paths)

- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox.cs — the toggle pattern (Crates/Bounty-style checkbox that grants prerequisites).
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Transforms.cs and TransformOnCapture.cs — the develop-one-tier verb.
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Capturable.cs, Captures.cs, GivesCashOnCapture.cs — the always-on territory-structures.
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/GrantConditionOnPrerequisite.cs and GrantConditionOnPlayerResources.cs — wiring Foothold thresholds to global capabilities.
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ScriptLobbyDropdown.cs — the Doctrine pick.
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/design/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/SupplyNetwork.cs — the existing prototype world-trait to model the Foothold counter on (integer-only, interval recompute, deterministic).
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/design/contemporary-openra-design.md — the parent design doc (CoH/Rise-of-Nations framing, ranked-toggle-for-diplomacy plan, Codex just-in-time onboarding) this layer should stay consistent with.

balance.executiveSummary:
The rejected Phase-0 test failed because territory REPLACED ore (income 0, derricks = 100% economy), which collapsed the game into a control-point map and killed the sacred harvester loop. The fix is structural, not numeric: ore must stay the felt "spine" — a self-sufficient (if weaker) economy on its own — and territory must be an AUGMENT layered on top, where MOST captured structures grant CAPABILITY (vision, repair, faster support-power charge, production, defense), not cash. Only a minority print credits, and those should be capped, capturable-back, and diminishing so they cannot snowball.

The triangle you want (EXPAND-to-ore / PROTECT-harvesters / FIGHT-for-map-control) is produced cheapest by MAP DESIGN, not by new systems: put safe-but-poor ore near each base (the spine that keeps an ignorer solvent) and rich-but-exposed ore plus the best capturable structures in the contested center (the carrot that pulls armies onto the map). The harvester's slow, killable, bounty-paying body is your built-in anti-snowball valve — a player who out-expands also exposes more harvesters to raids, and RA's existing GivesBounty trait pays the raider.

Concrete starting split to playtest: ore ~60% of a developed player's income, territory ~40%, of which only ~half (~20% of total) is direct cash — the rest is capability. Keep stock ore values (Ore 25/unit, 500-credit harvester load) untouched; that is the spine. Add ~6-10 capturable structures per 1v1 map, of which only 2-4 are "resource" type at a capped ~8-14 cr/sec each with diminishing returns past the third held. Everything is buildable in mod-data plus the existing CashTrickler / Capturable / SupplyNode / GivesBounty traits — no engine rewrite. The metric that proves it: a player who never captures a structure should still field a complete army (~70-80% of a territory-player's economy), and no single early map-control lead should let one side both out-economy AND out-fight.
keyFindings: ROOT CAUSE of the Phase-0 rejection, restated precisely: setting ore to 0 didn't just remove cash — it removed the *loop* (scout ore, plant a refinery forward, defend the harvester on its trip home, deny the enemy's). With that gone, the only economic verb left was 'stand on a point,' which is King-of-the-Hill. The lesson is that the harvester loop is content, not just income; territory must be added to it, never substituted for it.

Ore must remain a COMPLETE economy in isolation. The explicit failure-test bar: a player who ignores every capturable structure must still afford a full tech tree and a real army — call it ~70-80% of what a territory-active player fields, NOT 'broke.' This is the difference between 'territory is a tempo/edge advantage you fight for' (good) and 'territory is the only way to not lose by default' (the rejected control-point game).

TERRITORY SHOULD MOSTLY PAY IN CAPABILITY, NOT CASH — this is the single most important anti-failure decision, and it directly answers the user's confirmed Decision #2 (heterogeneous structures). If most captures printed credits you get a 'second wallet' and the control-point game returns. If most captures grant a *power* (forward vision, a repair pad, faster support-power charge, a free production queue, a defensive turret line), then holding ground changes HOW you fight without simply giving you a bigger bank — capability advantages are self-limiting (a repair pad is only worth its repair, it doesn't compound into infinite money) where cash advantages compound.

Company of Heroes is the cautionary tale the user already intuited: CoH ties ~all income to map points with no player input, and the community's two loudest complaints are (a) snowball — the early map-control winner out-resources AND out-fights, and stockpiled fuel lets a pushed-back player still afford the next tank, and (b) 'zero reason to take territory' moments where cutting sectors isn't rewarding enough. Both are symptoms of cash-from-points being the WHOLE economy. Keeping ore as a parallel, raid-vulnerable, expansion-driven income is precisely what CoH lacks and what prevents both failure modes.

StarCraft 2 gives the cleanest natural anti-snowball brake: mineral saturation. The first ~16 workers on a base earn ~57 min/worker/min; workers 17-24 earn only ~22 each — a built-in diminishing return that FORCES expansion onto contested ground rather than rewarding turtling on one rich base. RA already has a soft version of this (a finite ore field depletes, and a refinery can only dock so many harvesters). Lean into it: make near-base ore patches small/poor so they saturate fast, pushing players outward — the cheapest possible way to manufacture the expand-vs-protect tension.

Age of Empires 2 relics are the model for the GOOD kind of cash structure: a relic gives ~80 gold/min (≈ one extra villager), there are only ~5 on a map, they're capturable, and crucially they're worth 'roughly one extra worker' — a meaningful but NON-DOMINANT bonus. The design rule to steal: a single captured resource-structure should be worth on the order of ONE harvester's income, not five. That keeps it a fight-worth-having without making it the economy. Massable trade (50 trade carts) is the counter-example of an income source that DOES snowball — avoid anything territory-based that scales without a hard cap.

The harvester's body is the engine's built-in equalizer and raiding hook, and it's already wired. Harvesters are slow, heavily-armored-but-unarmed, and travel a predictable route — RA's whole 'harvester hunting' meta exists because killing one denies ~500 credits of in-transit value plus rebuild time. The engine ships GivesBounty (pays the killer) and the harvester is already a GivesBounty-able actor. This means the PROTECT-harvesters leg of the triangle needs zero new code: aggressive raiding is rewarded, and the out-expander who fields more harvesters exposes more of them — an automatic brake on the expansion snowball.

Every mechanism needed already exists as a reusable trait — this is mod-data plus trivial C#, matching the user's constraint. CashTrickler (flat condition-gated income, already used by the stock Oil Derrick at 100cr/375 ticks ≈ 6.7 cr/sec), Capturable + CaptureManager (capture-back), GivesCashOnCapture (one-time capture bonus), GivesBounty (raid reward), and the Phase-0 SupplyNetwork/SupplyNode traits (gate income on connectivity) cover the entire hybrid. Repurpose SupplyNode so it gates the *territory bonus* on being connected, NOT the whole economy — that's the one-line conceptual change from Phase 0.
recommendations: KEEP STOCK ORE VALUES EXACTLY — this is the spine, do not touch it. Ore 25/unit, Gems 50/unit, harvester capacity 20 (= 500 credits/full load), MaxDensity 12. A mid-distance harvester cycle sustains roughly 12-18 cr/sec. Two harvesters on a normal field ≈ 25-35 cr/sec, which is a complete RA economy by itself. The whole point is that this number alone keeps an ignorer solvent. The territory layer is added ON TOP of an unmodified harvester economy.

TARGET SPLIT TO PLAYTEST (not final): for a player actively contesting the map, ore ~60% / territory ~40% of total income. Critically, of that 40% territory share, only about HALF should be direct cash (~20% of total) and half should be capability (~20%-equivalent). So a fully-territorial player runs ~60% ore-cash + ~20% territory-cash + ~20% capability-edge; a player who IGNORES territory entirely still runs at ~60/80 ≈ 75% of the territory-player's economy. That 75% floor is the explicit 'not broke' guarantee. If playtesting shows the ignorer falls below ~65%, shift more weight back to ore (raise structure cost or lower their trickle).

HETEROGENEOUS STRUCTURE MIX per 1v1 map — ship ~6-10 capturable structures, but only 2-4 of them are 'resource' type. Concrete starting roster: (RESOURCE) 2-4x Oil Derrick clones via CashTrickler at ~8-14 cr/sec each (one ≈ a single harvester, the AoE-relic rule); (CAPABILITY) 1x Forward Radar (reveals a chunk of map / shroud), 1x Repair Depot (RepairsUnits aura), 1x Tech/Production outpost (grants a prerequisite or a free low-tier production queue), 1x Support-Power Relay (speeds your superweapon/support charge via a condition), 1x Defense Bastion (pre-built turret line you inherit on capture). The cash ones are the minority by design — capability is the territory payoff's center of gravity.

BUILD FOUR HARD BRAKES INTO THE CASH STRUCTURES so territory cannot snowball: (1) DIMINISHING RETURNS — each additional resource-structure a player holds pays less; e.g. 1st = 14 cr/sec, 2nd = 12, 3rd = 10, 4th+ = 6 (implement via a per-player count condition gating different CashTrickler amounts, or a simple stepped trait). (2) CAPTURABLE-BACK — all are Capturable, so a lead is never locked in; cutting/flipping a structure is a real attack vector (reuse SupplyNode connectivity so a flipped relay also de-supplies everything downstream). (3) HARD CAP — total territory cash should never exceed the ~40% target even at max capture; cap the resource-structure count or their summed output. (4) ORE AS EQUALIZER — because ore scales with expansion+defense skill and is raid-vulnerable, a behind player can still out-harvest a turtling map-leader, the comeback lane CoH lacks.

PREFER ORE-AMPLIFIER STRUCTURES OVER FLAT-CASH ones where you can — they reinforce the loop instead of bypassing it. A captured 'Logistics Depot' that gives +15% harvester unload speed or +1 effective harvester dock, or a 'Survey Station' that boosts field yield/regrow in a radius, ROUTES its value THROUGH the harvester loop: the bonus only pays if you're actually harvesting and protecting harvesters, so it deepens the spine rather than competing with it. Flat CashTrickler cash is fine for 1-2 'Oil Derrick' nostalgia structures, but make amplifiers the more common 'economic' capture. This is the cleanest way to make territory feel like it AUGMENTS harvesting, per the corrected thesis.

MANUFACTURE THE TRIANGLE THROUGH MAP DESIGN — it's free and it's the highest-leverage lever. Three ore tiers by position: (a) SAFE-POOR ore in each player's base pocket — small, saturates fast (small MaxDensity footprint), guarantees the spine but runs dry, forcing expansion; (b) MEDIUM ore at naturals/expansions — the bread-and-butter, defensible but exposed to raids; (c) RICH-CONTESTED ore (and Gems) in the center, co-located with the best capability structures so the SAME ground satisfies all three triangle legs at once. Co-locating rich ore + a Repair Depot + a Radar in the contested center is what makes one fight simultaneously about expansion, protection, and map control.

WIRE HARVESTER RAIDING AS A FIRST-CLASS LANE using existing traits: put GivesBounty on harvesters (killing one pays the raider ~10-15% of its value, on top of denying the ~500-credit load + rebuild time), and ensure base-pocket ore is defensible while expansion ore is not. This makes the PROTECT leg active: the out-expander has more harvesters on more exposed routes, so aggression scales with the leader's greed — a self-correcting anti-snowball. Do NOT add the cuttable supply-chain mechanic now (user put it on hold); the connectivity rule on territory structures already gives you a lighter 'cut the relay' play.

INSTRUMENT THESE METRICS every playtest, mapped to the failure modes: (1) IGNORER ECONOMY RATIO — income of a no-capture player vs a full-capture player; target ~0.70-0.80, alarm if <0.65 (territory became mandatory = control-point game returning) or >0.90 (territory is pointless). (2) SNOWBALL INDEX — does the player who holds the most territory at minute 8 also have the larger army at minute 15 AND win >~60%? If yes, brakes are too weak. (3) TERRITORY CASH SHARE — measure actual % of income from structures; should land ~20% direct cash, alarm if it creeps toward CoH's ~100%. (4) CAMERA-TIME-ON-ARMY (Phase-0's own metric) — should rise vs stock RA without the harvester loop disappearing from the camera. (5) HARVESTER-DEATHS-PER-MATCH — confirms the protect leg is live, not ignorable.
risks: SNOWBALL is the #1 risk and it's the documented CoH failure: whoever wins early map control out-economies AND out-fights, compounding into an unrecoverable lead. Even with ore kept as a parallel economy, if the cash-structure trickle is too high or uncapped, the map leader's extra cash buys the army that holds the map that pays the cash. MITIGATION: the four brakes (diminishing returns, capturable-back, hard cap, ore-as-equalizer) plus a STRICT ceiling on total territory cash. Watch the Snowball Index metric; if a minute-8 territory lead predicts the win >60%, cut structure income before anything else.

OVER-CORRECTION back into irrelevance: if you make territory too weak/too capability-only/too cheap to ignore, players rationally skip it and you've spent design budget on a system nobody fights for — the inverse failure. The ~40% territory share and ~6-10 structures/map exist to keep it worth fighting for. The Ignorer Economy Ratio guards both directions: <0.65 = mandatory (bad), >0.90 = pointless (also bad).

CAPABILITY STRUCTURES ARE HARDER TO BALANCE THAN CASH because their value is matchup- and situation-dependent (a Repair Depot is huge for an armor army, marginal for air; a Radar is huge vs a sneaky faction, marginal vs a brawler). A capability structure that's worth ~0 to one faction and game-winning to another reintroduces the combinatorial-balance problem the parent design already flagged. MITIGATION: give each capability structure a baseline universal value (small flat utility) so it's never dead, and lean on capturable-back so a mis-valued structure self-corrects through contestation.

DIMINISHING-RETURNS ON CASH STRUCTURES IS FIDDLY TO IMPLEMENT DETERMINISTICALLY — a per-player 'count of held resource-structures' condition that re-evaluates on every capture/loss must be lockstep-safe (integer-only, no float, evaluated in sim). It's doable with existing condition/CashTrickler machinery but it's the one piece that needs real C# care, not just YAML. MITIGATION: prototype the stepped-amount version first (discrete CashTrickler conditions per count bracket) rather than a continuous curve; it's trivially deterministic and good enough to playtest.

THE TWO-WALLET PERCEPTION can creep back even with a minority of cash structures if their UI/feedback makes 'capture = money' the salient mental model. If players learn 'derricks = the economy,' you've re-created the rejected game psychologically even if the numbers say otherwise. MITIGATION: make the FIRST and most visible captures be capability (vision, repair), introduce cash structures as the rarer 'jackpot,' and ensure the harvester income readout stays the dominant on-screen economic signal.

MAP-DESIGN DEPENDENCY: this whole triangle leans heavily on hand-placed ore tiers and structure positions. A badly-tuned map (rich ore too safe, or all structures clustered) collapses the triangle regardless of the numbers. The Phase-0 Lua auto-placer that sprays nodes in spokes is NOT sufficient for the hybrid — it needs deliberate safe-poor/medium/rich-contested zoning. MITIGATION: hand-author 2-3 reference 1v1 maps for the hybrid before trusting any auto-placer; treat map design as part of the balance surface, not set-dressing.

DETERMINISM in the income path: any per-tick territory income, diminishing-returns count, or bounty payout reached from world.Tick() must use fixed-point/integer math and synced fields only. CashTrickler/GivesBounty are already sim-safe, but a custom diminishing-returns aggregator is new code in the hot path. MITIGATION: keep all territory-income math integer, mark synced fields [Sync], and run the determinism/replay check (the parent roadmap's Phase-1 spike) over a territory-heavy match.

precedents.name: Company of Heroes 1/2 — territory points as the whole economy
precedents.whatTheyDid: Almost all income (fuel, munitions, partly manpower) comes from capturing connected territory points with no player input; cutting a point in the supply chain isolates and de-resources everything downstream.
precedents.outcome: Mixed: the map-IS-the-economy idea is genuinely strategic and proven, but the community's two loudest complaints are (a) snowball — the early map winner out-resources and out-fights, and stockpiled fuel lets even a pushed-back player afford the next tank, and (b) 'zero reason to take territory' moments where cutting sectors isn't rewarding enough because manpower (the key resource) isn't tied to territory.
precedents.lessonForUs: This IS the rejected Phase-0 model at AAA scale — proof that cash-from-points as the WHOLE economy snowballs and drifts. Our fix is exactly what CoH lacks: a parallel, expansion-driven, raid-vulnerable ore economy that a behind player can out-grind, plus making most captures pay capability not cash.

precedents.name: StarCraft 2 — mineral saturation diminishing returns
precedents.whatTheyDid: First ~16 workers on a base earn ~57 min/worker/min; workers 17-24 earn only ~22 each, so a saturated base is far less efficient than a fresh expansion.
precedents.outcome: Gold-standard anti-snowball/expansion driver: it makes spreading onto contested ground mathematically necessary rather than optional, without any explicit 'comeback' mechanic — the economy itself pushes you out and exposes you.
precedents.lessonForUs: Make near-base ore small/poor so it saturates and depletes fast, forcing expansion to medium/rich fields in contested space. This manufactures the expand-vs-protect tension through map+resource tuning alone — the cheapest lever — and gives the same natural brake without bolting on artificial diminishing returns to ore.

precedents.name: Age of Empires 2 — relics
precedents.whatTheyDid: ~5 capturable relics per map, each garrisoned for ~80 gold/min (≈ one extra gold villager), contestable and stealable; civ bonuses tweak relic value modestly.
precedents.outcome: A well-loved, well-balanced 'fight over the map for income' system precisely because each relic is worth ~one worker — meaningful but non-dominant — and they're hard-capped at ~5, so they never become the economy.
precedents.lessonForUs: The exact template for our cash structures: one captured resource-structure ≈ one harvester's income (not five), hard-capped count, capturable-back. This keeps them a fight-worth-having without recreating the second-wallet/control-point failure. Massable trade carts (which DO snowball) are the anti-pattern to avoid — never let territory income scale uncapped.

precedents.name: Red Alert (own game) — ore/gems + harvester hunting
precedents.whatTheyDid: Ore (25/unit) is the bread-and-butter; Gems (50/unit) are a richer, scarcer, usually more-contested deposit; harvesters are slow, armored, unarmed, predictable-route vehicles, and 'harvester hunting' (killing the ~500-credit load in transit) is a core meta — RA3 even added Burst Drones that cut refinery output ~28%.
precedents.outcome: A 25-year-proven economy whose tension comes entirely from where the ore is and whether you can protect the harvester on its trip — fast, readable, twitchy, and the thing the user explicitly wants to preserve.
precedents.lessonForUs: This is the spine — keep it untouched. Gems already ARE the 'rich-contested center' template; lean on that for map zoning. Harvester hunting + the existing GivesBounty trait give the PROTECT leg for free. Territory is the new third leg ADDED to this, never a replacement for it.

precedents.name: Phase-0 THEATER prototype (the rejected test)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Set ore/gems to 0 and made supply-connected Control Nodes (Oil Derrick clones at 35 cr/sec, gated on a flood-filled supply chain back to the CY) 100% of income.
precedents.outcome: REJECTED in playtest: harvesting felt meaningless, derricks became the only economic objective, and it drifted into a control-point game that lost what makes RA fun — exactly the CoH failure mode at prototype scale.
precedents.lessonForUs: The SupplyNetwork/SupplyNode/CashTrickler tech it built is reusable and good — the only change is conceptual: keep ore at full value, and re-gate the supply chain so it controls the ~20% territory-cash BONUS, not the whole economy. Same code, inverted ratio, plus a capability-heavy structure mix. Don't throw away Phase-0's engine work; re-point it.

balance.detail:
# THEATER — Making the 60/40 Ore-Territory Hybrid Produce the Triangle

## 0. The one-sentence fix for why Phase-0 failed
Phase-0 didn't fail because the *numbers* were wrong; it failed because it deleted the harvester **loop** (scout ore → forward-refine → defend the trip home → deny the enemy's) and left only "stand on a point." The corrected design keeps that entire loop at full strength and **adds** a territory layer on top of it. Reuse Phase-0's SupplyNetwork/SupplyNode/CashTrickler code verbatim — just re-point it from "the economy" to "a ~20% cash bonus + capability."

## 1. Ore as the felt spine (the "not broke" guarantee)
- Keep stock values: **Ore 25/unit, Gems 50/unit, harvester capacity 20 (= 500 cr/full load), MaxDensity 12.** Do not touch these.
- A mid-distance harvester sustains ~12-18 cr/sec; two harvesters ≈ 25-35 cr/sec — a complete RA economy alone.
- **Bar to hold:** a player who captures NOTHING runs at ~70-80% of a full-territory player's economy. That is "weaker but complete," not "broke." This single ratio is the whole difference between the corrected design and the rejected one.

## 2. The split to playtest (starting point, not final)
For a player actively contesting the map:
- **~60% ore-cash** (harvesters) — the spine.
- **~20% territory-cash** (a MINORITY of structures) — direct credits.
- **~20% capability** (the MAJORITY of structures) — vision/repair/production/defense/support-charge, valued as economy-equivalent.

Ignorer math: 60 / (60+20) = **0.75** economy ratio vs the territory player → on target. If the ignorer dips below ~0.65 in testing, territory has become mandatory (control-point game returning) → raise structure cost or cut their trickle. If above ~0.90, territory is pointless → raise structure value or add a capability that matters.

## 3. The structure roster (heterogeneous, capability-heavy) — per 1v1 map
Ship ~6-10 capturable structures; only **2-4 are cash**:

| Type | Structure | Payoff | Engine trait | Starting number |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CASH | Oil Derrick clone | flat credits | `CashTrickler` | 8-14 cr/sec each, 2-4/map |
| CASH-AMPLIFIER (preferred) | Logistics Depot / Survey Station | +harvester unload speed or +field yield in radius | condition + existing harvester/resource modifiers | 1-2/map |
| CAPABILITY | Forward Radar | reveals map chunk / shroud | `RevealsShroud` aura on capture | 1/map |
| CAPABILITY | Repair Depot | repairs nearby units | `RepairsUnits` aura | 1/map |
| CAPABILITY | Production Outpost | grants prereq / free low-tier queue | prerequisite condition | 1/map |
| CAPABILITY | Support Relay | speeds support-power charge | condition feeding power timer | 1/map |
| CAPABILITY | Defense Bastion | inherited turret line | pre-built turrets, `Capturable` | 0-1/map |

**Rule of thumb (from AoE relics):** one cash structure ≈ ONE harvester's income, never five. Prefer **amplifiers** (route value through the harvester loop, so they deepen the spine) over flat cash (which bypasses it). Make the *first/most-visible* captures capability, so players never learn "capture = money."

## 4. The four anti-snowball brakes (this is where CoH failed)
1. **Diminishing returns on cash structures** — 1st=14, 2nd=12, 3rd=10, 4th+=6 cr/sec. Implement as stepped CashTrickler conditions keyed on a per-player held-count (integer/sim-safe; prototype discrete brackets, not a continuous curve).
2. **Capturable-back** — everything is `Capturable`; reuse SupplyNode connectivity so flipping a relay de-supplies everything downstream (the light "cut the chain" play — the heavier cuttable supply-chain stays on hold per your decision).
3. **Hard cap** — total territory cash never exceeds the ~40% target even at full capture; cap structure count or summed output.
4. **Ore as the equalizer** — ore scales with expansion+defense *skill* and is raid-vulnerable, so a behind player can out-grind a turtling map-leader. This is the comeback lane CoH structurally lacks.

## 5. Map design IS the triangle (free, highest leverage)
Three ore tiers by position:
- **Safe-poor** in each base pocket — small footprint, saturates/depletes fast (SC2 saturation logic) → guarantees the spine but **forces expansion**.
- **Medium** at naturals — defensible but raidable; bread-and-butter.
- **Rich-contested center** — gems + the best capability structures **co-located**, so the SAME ground is simultaneously the expand, protect, and map-control objective.

Co-locating rich ore + Repair Depot + Radar in the center is what makes one teamfight about all three triangle legs at once. **Hand-author 2-3 reference maps**; the Phase-0 spoke auto-placer is not sufficient for zoned hybrid maps.

## 6. Harvester raiding / bounty (the PROTECT leg, free)
- Put `GivesBounty` on harvesters (~10-15% of value to the killer) on top of the ~500-cr denied load + rebuild time.
- Base-pocket ore defensible; expansion ore exposed. The out-expander fields more harvesters on more exposed routes → aggression scales with the leader's greed → automatic anti-snowball. Zero new code.

## 7. Implementation surface (mod-data + trivial C#)
All reusable, already in-repo: `CashTrickler` (stock Oil Derrick = 100cr/375 ticks ≈ 6.7 cr/sec is your reference), `Capturable`+`CaptureManager`, `GivesCashOnCapture` (one-time capture bonus), `GivesBounty`, and Phase-0's `SupplyNetwork`/`SupplyNode`. The ONLY meaningfully new C# is the deterministic diminishing-returns aggregator (keep it integer, `[Sync]`, sim-side). 25 ticks/sec at RA normal speed for all cr/sec math.

## 8. Metrics to watch (mapped to failure modes)
| Metric | Target | Alarm |
|---|---|---|
| Ignorer economy ratio | 0.70-0.80 | <0.65 (mandatory) or >0.90 (pointless) |
| Snowball index (min-8 territory lead → win%) | <~55-60% | >60% → brakes too weak |
| Territory cash share of income | ~20% | creeping toward CoH's ~100% |
| Camera-time-on-army (Phase-0 metric) | up vs stock RA | harvester loop vanishing from camera |
| Harvester deaths/match | >0, meaningful | ~0 → protect leg is ignorable |

## 9. What NOT to do (your confirmed constraints)
- Don't set ore to 0 (the rejected thesis).
- Don't make most structures pay cash (second-wallet → control-point game).
- Don't add the cuttable supply-chain now (on hold) — the connectivity-flip on relays gives a lighter version for free.
- Don't trust the auto-placer for hybrid maps — hand-zone safe-poor / medium / rich-contested.
- Don't let any territory income scale uncapped (the AoE trade-cart anti-pattern).

**Sources:** Wayward Strategy & Callum McCole anti-snowball design essays; CoH2 community economy/snowball threads (steamcommunity.com); SC2 mineral-saturation mechanics (gamereplays.org, battle.net); AoE2 relic economics (ageofempires.fandom.com, aoezone.net); C&C harvester-hunting wiki + RA3 economy guides (cnc.fandom.com, gamereplays.org). Engine anchors verified in-repo: mods/ra/rules/player.yaml (ResourceValues Ore 25 / Gems 50), vehicles.yaml (harvester capacity 20), civilian.yaml (OILB CashTrickler 100/375), world.yaml (MaxDensity), mod.yaml (Timestep 40 = 25 ticks/sec), and OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/{CashTrickler,Capturable,GivesBounty,GivesCashOnCapture}.cs.

design.economyModel: HYBRID with ore as the untouched "spine" and territory layered on top as a minority cash + majority capability augment. Stock ore values stay EXACTLY as-is (verified mods/ra/rules/player.yaml:4-6 = Ore: 25, Gems: 50; HARV Capacity 20 = 500cr/load, mods/ra/rules/vehicles.yaml:330). The harvester LOOP (scout ore -> forward-refine -> defend the trip home -> deny the enemy's) is the sacred content we preserve; Phase-0's fatal error was deleting the loop (ore->0), not mis-tuning a number. So: do NOT lower ore at all. Territory income is purely additive on top of a full-strength harvester economy. The corrected thesis "territory AUGMENTS harvesting" is enforced structurally, not just by ratio: the preferred economic structures are AMPLIFIERS that route their value THROUGH the harvester loop (they pay nothing if you've stopped harvesting), so they reward the spine instead of competing with it. Hard design law: PERSISTENCE/VALUE lives in CAPABILITY (who you are, what you can do); the ore loop is where CAPITAL is earned and re-earned. The non-negotiable bar: a player who captures NOTHING must still field a complete tech tree + real army at ~70-80% of a full-territory player's economy ("weaker but complete," never "broke"). That ~0.75 floor is the line between "territory is an edge you fight for" (good) and "territory is the only way to not lose by default" (the rejected control-point game).
design.economySplit: Target for a player actively contesting the map: ORE ~60% of income, TERRITORY ~40% — but of that 40%, only ~half is direct cash (~20% of total) and ~half is capability-equivalent (~20%). So a fully-territorial player runs ~60% ore-cash + ~20% territory-cash + ~20% capability-edge. Ignorer math: 60/(60+20) = ~0.75 economy ratio vs the territory player — on the floor by design. STARTING NUMBERS TO PLAYTEST (all reusing CashTrickler; stock OILB reference = 100cr/375 ticks ~= 6.7 cr/sec at the verified 25 ticks/sec Timestep 40): cash structures pay ~8-14 cr/sec each (one cash node ~= ONE harvester's income — the AoE2-relic rule, never five). Diminishing returns on cash nodes per player: 1st=14, 2nd=12, 3rd=10, 4th+=6 cr/sec. Hard cap total territory-cash at the ~20%-of-total ceiling even at max capture. Keep ore values stock (Ore 25 / Gems 50, capacity 20). KILL-GATE METRICS each playtest: (1) Ignorer-economy-ratio target 0.70-0.80; alarm <0.65 (territory became mandatory = control-point game returning) or >0.90 (territory pointless). (2) Snowball index: minute-8 territory leader's win% should be <~55-60%; >60% = brakes too weak. (3) Territory-cash share ~20%; alarm if it creeps toward CoH's ~100%. (4) Camera-time-on-army up vs stock RA WITHOUT the harvester loop leaving the camera. (5) Harvester-deaths/match > 0 and meaningful (confirms the PROTECT leg is live).
design.territoryStructures: Ship ~6-10 capturable structures per 1v1 map but only 2-4 are cash — capability is the center of gravity. The structures are ALWAYS-ON regardless of the civ toggle (they're just RA tech buildings; OpenRA already ships fights over OILB/HOSP/DOME). All reuse stock traits + Capturable/CaptureManager/OwnerLostAction(ChangeOwner)/CapturableProgressBar; every entry reskins an existing RA sprite (zero new 32-facing art). ROSTER: ECONOMIC (minority, 2-4/map): (1) Oil Derrick [OILB] — the lone classic flat trickle, CashTrickler tuned low (~8-14 cr/sec), kept for nostalgia/tempo; (2) Refinery Concession [reskin OILB/TECN] — ore-VALUE AMPLIFIER: on capture an owner-scoped ProvidesPrerequisite -> player GrantConditionOnPrerequisite -> player-level ResourceValueMultiplier (+15-25% cash-per-ore). Pays ZERO if you aren't harvesting — welds territory to the spine; (3) Foundry/War Plant [reskin TECN] — ProductionCostMultiplier (-10-15% unit cost), an amplifier on the OUTPUT side. PREFER these amplifiers over flat cash because they reinforce the loop. POWER (majority): (4) Watchtower/Listening Post [DOME/comms reskin] — RevealsShroud over a choke/ore route; (5) Field Hospital [HOSP, stock] — infantry heal aura via ProximityExternalCondition; (6) Service Depot/Repair Bay [FIX, stock RepairsUnits] — forward vehicle repair; (7) Radar Outpost [DOME] — DetectCloaked (hard counter to subs/spies, LOCATIONAL); (8) Forward Command [FCOM, already has GivesBuildableArea + BaseProvider] — extends buildable area = the "develop the ground / Foothold-not-Empire" verb in physical form; (9) Reinforcement Depot — Production forward-exit or timed free-unit drip; (10) Tech Center/Relay [TECN] — the single map "relic": ProvidesPrerequisite tech unlock + support-power charge accel. NEW C# (only two, ~40 lines each, both ConditionalTrait subclasses mirroring ResourceValueMultiplier/ReloadDelayMultiplier): a SupportPower ChargeRateMultiplier (verified: SupportPower.cs:21 ChargeInterval is a static field with NO modifier interface) and a gated/owner-scoped SeedsResource wrapper for an optional ore-field-enrichment "Prospecting Station" (integer cell-tick, deterministic). Everything else is mod-data. MAP RECIPE: never all 10, never many copies of one; spread so no two adjacent objectives reward the same verb (the explicit cure for the repeated-control-point drift), with exactly ONE Tech Center as the central high-stakes node.
design.theTriangle: EXPAND-to-richer-ore <-> PROTECT-your-harvesters <-> FIGHT-for-map-control, all competing for the same attention at RA pace. The triangle is manufactured primarily by MAP DESIGN (free, highest-leverage), not by new systems. Three ore tiers by POSITION: (a) SAFE-POOR ore in each base pocket — small footprint, saturates/depletes fast (lean on RA's existing finite-field + dock-cap, the SC2-saturation lesson), guaranteeing the spine but FORCING expansion; (b) MEDIUM ore at naturals — defensible but raid-exposed, the bread-and-butter; (c) RICH-CONTESTED ore + Gems in the center, CO-LOCATED with the best capability structures (Repair Depot + Radar + Tech Center) so the SAME ground simultaneously satisfies all three legs — one fight is at once about expansion, protection, and control. HOW THE NUMBERS CREATE IT: ore stays the major income, so EXPAND matters; the harvester is slow/armored/unarmed on a predictable route and carries ~500cr in transit, so PROTECT matters — and crucially the out-expander fields MORE harvesters on MORE exposed routes, making aggression scale with the leader's greed (automatic anti-snowball). The capability structures (vision/repair/charge) change HOW you fight at the contested center, so FIGHT-for-control matters and pays in capability not a second wallet. HARVESTER RAIDING is wired as a first-class lane for FREE via the verified stock GivesBounty trait on harvesters (pays the raider ~10-15% on top of the denied load + rebuild time). Verified-present traits make this mod-data: GivesBounty.cs, CashTrickler.cs, Capturable.cs, plus Phase-0's SupplyNode.cs / World/SupplyNetwork.cs to gate the territory BONUS on connectivity (the light "cut the relay" play — NOT the full cuttable supply-chain, which is on hold).
design.matchCivLayer: ONE legible verb on top of always-on structures, capped at ~3-4 discrete decisions per 40-min match, MAP-ANCHORED (no second panel/city screen). The whole match civ layer is exactly three things, NOT a system: (1) DEVELOP-ONE-TIER: a structure you currently hold exposes a single "Develop" command — pay credits + a build delay, it visibly upgrades its banner/sprite and steps up its single payoff (richer income / longer vision / faster charge). Implemented with the existing Transforms/TransformOnCapture pattern. ONE tier only in a match, ever — no tier 2/3 ladder. The credit cost competes with army spend (Sid-Meier "interesting choice": develop the node OR build two tanks, never both), which is what stops it being free mandatory value. (2) ONE FOOTHOLD METER: a single 0-100 bar fed PASSIVELY by how much developed territory you hold, crossing at most TWO thresholds per match, each granting one global passive via GrantConditionOnPrerequisite (e.g. 50%: developed structures self-repair; 100%: one extra build queue or a faction power). It is STATE, never spent — no second wallet. Modeled on the verified World/SupplyNetwork.cs (integer-only, interval recompute, [Sync]ed; deterministic). (3) ONE DOCTRINE PICK: a single irreversible identity fork (Economic / Military / Civic-Support) made once, surfaced just-in-time when Foothold first ticks up — recolors what "develop" MEANS for you. Not a tech tree. PSYCHOLOGY GUARD (the real constraint): "optional" dies the instant the optimal player MUST micro it, so every develop action is one-time set-and-forget (seconds of attention per several minutes, never per-tick/per-unit) AND payoff is a SIDEGRADE/identity more than a bigger number — tuned for ATTENTION-NEUTRALITY (a develop-blind clean-RA player should beat a develop-heavy player ~50/50; if develop-heavy wins >60%, the layer is mandatory APM and must be flattened). PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: minute one is pure RA; the Develop verb isn't even offered until the player's FIRST capture (one just-in-time line, then silence); the Doctrine prompt appears only at first Foothold gain.
design.matchToggle: ONE lobby checkbox "Develop Territory" via the verified LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox.cs (literally the Crates/Bounty pattern — grants prerequisites when ticked). CRITICAL SEPARATION — the toggle does NOT gate the structures: the heterogeneous capturable structures (resource AND power) are ALWAYS present and capturable in both states because a capturable tech building is core RA. The toggle gates ONLY the thin develop layer on top. OFF = capture a structure, get its static reward, full stop — byte-identical map/structures/capture game to ON, so the toggle physically CANNOT fork balance at the level of map control. ON = held structures expose the single Develop command, and the Foothold meter + one Doctrine pick become active. This is the clean answer to "does the toggle fork the community": it's additive "RA-plus-a-bit," not a different game. DEFAULTS/LOCKING (the SC2-coop-vs-1v1 lesson, the inverse of the Fortnite no-build split): LOCKED OFF in ranked 1v1 (keep ONE canonical competitive surface to balance, exactly as the design doc already plans for diplomacy); DEFAULT ON in skirmish-vs-AI / co-op / comp-stomp where the depth-seeking audience lives; a normal toggle in custom lobbies. The develop layer deliberately gets NO ranked ladder of its own. NON-PERSISTENT: the developed structures and the dossier/Foothold state die at match end — persistence is campaign-only.
design.campaignCivLayer: HEAVIER, persistent "you develop a nation" lean modeled on Dawn of War: Dark Crusade x XCOM x Homeworld — NOT Total War/Stellaris. The ONE LAW: PERSISTENCE = CAPABILITY (who you are / who survived), RESET = CAPITAL (money, base, mass army, mission-map control). Cap the persistent set at exactly FOUR pillars you can NAME, never AUDIT (if something new wants to persist it must REPLACE a pillar, not add): (1) THE COMMANDER — one unique named hero that carries level (via the verified stock GainsExperience.cs) + a few unlocked "Wargear" (each = a granted engine condition). The cheapest, highest-emotional-ROI piece; build FIRST. (2) THE VETERAN CADRE — 3-6 units HARD-CAPPED; at mission end you pick which SURVIVORS to extract (XCOM roster + Homeworld fleet emotion + Dark Crusade Honor Guard). They return as pre-veteran reinforcements (ProductionFromMapEdge/Paradrop + ProducibleWithLevel). The cap is the anti-snowball governor; cadre units can die permanently, the mass army cannot persist and stays expendable. (3) THE NATION DOSSIER — 3-5 identity perks (the "civ" layer), each ONE engine condition / Buildable prerequisite granted at mission start, UNLOCKED BY HOW YOU PLAYED (capture all derricks -> "Industrialist"; protect all harvesters -> "Logistics Corps"; finish fast -> "Blitz"). Perks are characterful SIDEGRADES (unlock a unit, change a node's payoff type, discount a power), NOT flat power, with diminishing returns — "develop-the-ground-as-identity" with ZERO per-mission management. (4) THE HOME THEATER — a tiny meta-map of <=10 liberated nodes ("Foothold not Empire"), with a small Reconstruction budget (earned from performance, NOT carried cash) buying at most ONE upgrade per interstitial (fortify a node so it starts pre-captured, or convert its payoff type). CRUCIAL: persist the HERO+ROSTER+IDENTITY (Dark Crusade) but RESET THE BASE every mission (the Soulstorm rule) — you always rebuild your tactical base from a Construction Yard, which protects the sacred RA loop AND kills the capital snowball. Built on the SAME perk/condition/dossier machinery as the match layer — the only difference is whether state is serialized.
design.campaignPersistence: THE MECHANISM (and the honest blocker): OpenRA campaigns are STATELESS chains of independent missions — verified, there is no carry-over of player tech/units/state. missions.yaml is a sequencing list; each map.yaml is self-contained; Lua runs only within its mission frame; D2K "upgrades" are hardcoded per-map, not persisted. So heavy persistence REQUIRES new C#: a small CampaignState blob (hero level + Wargear, cadre roster, dossier perks, home-region node state, mission index) serialized to disk at mission end (hook INotifyGameEnd) and RE-INJECTED at the next mission's start as PRE-GAME actor inits + Ruleset/granted-condition modifications — the same path mods already use — NEVER as runtime mutation of synced state, so determinism rules don't bite (single-player is the safe initial target; co-op needs CampaignState loaded identically on all clients pre-game). HONEST COST: this is the one genuine architectural gap, ~200-400 LOC C# + a thin between-missions UI, plus a save-location decision (per-campaign file vs player profile). RECOMMENDATION: do NOT build it for Phase 1 — flag it as a separate scoped task; MATCHES (non-persistent) ships first. PROTOTYPE PATH that validates the one question cheaply (zero new art, reskin an existing hero like Tanya): serialize ONLY the persistent Commander (one GainsExperience unit) + a 3-perk dossier across two stitched skirmish missions, and answer "does 'my commander leveled and my nation became Industrialist' feel like meaningful DEVELOPMENT without feeling like HOMEWORK?" Only if that hooks do you add the cadre, then the Theater-map Reconstruction screen. Do NOT build the full meta-map first — that's the piece most likely to drift into the 4X tax.
antiTrapGuards: FOUR ANTI-SNOWBALL BRAKES on territory cash (the documented CoH failure): (1) diminishing returns per held cash-node 14/12/10/6 cr/sec; (2) everything Capturable-back so a lead is never locked; (3) hard cap on total territory-cash at the ~20%-of-total ceiling; (4) ore-as-equalizer — ore scales with expansion+defense SKILL and is raid-vulnerable, so a behind player can out-grind a turtling map-leader (the comeback lane CoH lacks).

ONE-WALLET RULE: develop is paid in CREDITS; Foothold is STATE that is never spent; territory mostly pays CAPABILITY not cash. Any new spendable counter is rejected on sight — this is what dodges the 'second wallet / control-point game' the user already rejected.

AMPLIFY-DON'T-DUPLICATE: prefer ResourceValueMultiplier/ProductionCostMultiplier structures whose value is ZERO if you stop harvesting/producing, structurally welding territory to the ore loop instead of replacing it.

ATTENTION-NEUTRALITY: develop-blind clean-RA player must win ~50/50 vs develop-heavy (alarm >60% = mandatory APM). Develop actions are set-and-forget (seconds per several minutes), never per-tick/per-unit; payoffs are sidegrades not bigger numbers.

CAP THE CHOICE BUDGET: ~3-4 discrete decisions per match (1 Doctrine + ~2-3 Develops + 2 Foothold thresholds). Any 5th/6th develop click means it's become APM — raise cost or add a per-match develop cap.
PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: minute one is pure RA; develop verb gated behind first capture; Doctrine gated behind first Foothold. The layer reveals itself only when relevant — no pre-game 4X system dump.

MAP-ANCHORED, NO MENUS: every develop action is clicked ON the battlefield structure and SEEN as a sprite/banner change. No off-map panel can pull the camera off the fight (the CoH/Rise-of-Nations property). Any request for scrollbars/sub-menus is a red flag to CUT, not expand.

CAMPAIGN PILLAR CAP: exactly 4 persistent pillars (Commander, Cadre<=6, Dossier<=5 perks, Home Theater<=10 nodes); new persistence must REPLACE a pillar. Reconstruction screen <=3 choices / <60 seconds.

ANTI-DEATH-SPIRAL FLOORS (the Homeworld trap the user named): hero is DOWNED-not-dead; guaranteed minimum starting force+base every mission; lost mission can be retried or routed-around (Dark Crusade); a floor below which persistent state cannot drop. Losing costs PROGRESS, never the RUN.

DIFFICULTY SCALES WITH CAMPAIGN PROGRESS, NOT PLAYER STRENGTH (Dark Crusade's stronghold stayed hard regardless of dominance), and NO visible rubber-banding (research is explicit players hate it) — scale enemy starting forces/objectives subtly, never nerf the player's persistent stuff. Act boundaries are deliberate RE-FLOOR points (WC3 Arthas gear reset).
design.pacePreservation: RA's fast/readable/twitchy pace is preserved by FIVE structural choices, not by hoping. (1) The sacred harvester loop runs at FULL strength every mission/match (ore stays stock; never set to 0) — the twitchy scout/refine/defend/deny content the user loves is the spine, untouched. (2) The economy RESETS each mission and starts near-broke, so the EXPAND/PROTECT/FIGHT triangle is RE-FOUGHT from zero every time — pace can't go stale into an attrition grind. (3) The civ layer is capped at ~3-4 low-frequency, set-and-forget decisions per match and is MAP-ANCHORED — no pause-to-think, no spreadsheet, no off-map UI to pull the camera off the fight; eyes stay on the battlefield BY DEFINITION (camera-time-on-army is an explicit kill-gate metric). (4) Progressive disclosure keeps minute-one pure Red Alert; the layer appears only when relevant. (5) Strategic depth comes from a few cross-coupling systems set as BACKGROUND STATE crossed BETWEEN fights (Rise of Nations / CoH model), never decisions made DURING a fight on the opponent's tempo — the moment the civ layer demands mid-fight attention it has failed and must be redesigned. Determinism/lockstep safety is maintained throughout: Foothold and all territory income use integer-only math, [Sync]ed fields, the Develop order routed through the normal IResolveOrder pipeline, and CampaignState loaded only as pre-game inits — verified that the existing SupplyNetwork.cs already does interval integer recompute, and that ChargeInterval is the only new sim-touching field, handled by an integer ConditionalTrait.
openQuestions: AMPLIFIER vs FLAT-CASH RATIO: how many of the 2-4 economic structures should be loop-amplifiers (ResourceValueMultiplier/ProductionCostMultiplier) vs flat CashTrickler derricks? Amplifiers best embody the corrected thesis but are invisible (no cash-tick feedback) and could feel unsatisfying; flat cash is legible but risks the second-wallet mental model. Needs playtest to find the mix that feels like augmentation, not a wallet.

DIMINISHING-RETURNS IMPLEMENTATION: the per-player held-cash-node count condition that re-evaluates on every capture/loss must be lockstep-safe. Prototype the discrete stepped-bracket version (trivially deterministic) — but confirm it doesn't desync under rapid recaptures, and decide whether brackets are per-player-global or per-structure.

CAPABILITY-STRUCTURE BALANCE: capability value is matchup-dependent (a Repair Depot is huge for armor, marginal for air; Radar huge vs subs/spies, marginal vs a brawler). Does each capability node need a small universal baseline so it's never a dead capture, and is capturable-back enough self-correction?

FOOTHOLD THRESHOLDS: what exactly do 50% and 100% grant so they feel game-defining but not snowbally? Self-repair + extra build queue are placeholders — need values that don't let the Foothold leader out-economy AND out-fight.

DOCTRINE COUNT/CONTENT: is three doctrines (Economic/Military/Civic) enough replay variety, and does an irreversible early pick create feel-bad when the map/matchup punishes it? Consider whether it should be re-pickable at a Foothold threshold.

MAP-AUTHORING BURDEN: the triangle leans on hand-zoned safe-poor/medium/rich-contested ore + deliberate structure placement; the Phase-0 spoke auto-placer is insufficient for hybrid maps. How many hand-authored reference 1v1 maps before trusting any auto-placer, and can symmetry be guaranteed?

CAMPAIGN PERSISTENCE SCOPE: what is the minimum viable CampaignState (just hero + 3 perks?) that proves the 'development without homework' feel, and where does the save live (per-campaign file vs player profile)? Co-op determinism of CampaignState load is unresolved.

SUPPORT-POWER CHARGE ACCELERATOR: the new ISupportPowerChargeModifier hook + ChargeRateMultiplier trait is the one genuinely new sim-touching C# — needs a determinism/replay check on a territory-heavy match before it's trusted.

ART DIFFERENTIATION: with 10 structures all reskinning ~5 RA sprites (OILB/HOSP/FIX/DOME/FCOM/TECN), can players read them apart at RA pace by tooltip + banner alone, or does legibility force cutting the roster down for a first prototype?
design.detail: SEQUENCING (what to build, in order, all verified mod-data + small C#): PHASE 1 (MATCHES, the main mode — zero new art, kill-gate first): (a) restore/keep stock ore — confirmed already Ore 25/Gems 50 in mods/ra/rules/player.yaml; the Phase-0 territory-economy.yaml that set ore->0 stays OPT-IN/unused. (b) Author the heterogeneous structure roster as inherited templates in a new mods/ra/rules/theater.yaml (e.g. ^CapturedIncomeNode, ^CapturedPowerNode — inherit, don't repeat, to avoid the RequiresCondition YAML balloon the research flags). Reskin OILB/HOSP/FIX/DOME/FCOM/TECN. (c) Wire the always-on capture game with stock Capturable/CaptureManager/GivesCashOnCapture/CashTrickler/RevealsShroud/RepairsUnits/DetectCloaked/GivesBuildableArea/BaseProvider/Production + GivesBounty on HARV. (d) Add the toggle via LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox (verified pattern), gating ONLY the develop layer. (e) Build the one Foothold world-trait (copy World/SupplyNetwork.cs's integer/interval/[Sync] shape) + a thin Develop order (IResolveOrder) + Transforms-based one-tier upgrade + ScriptLobbyDropdown Doctrine pick. (f) The two new ~40-line ConditionalTraits: ChargeRateMultiplier (SupportPower.cs:21 ChargeInterval has no modifier — confirmed) and the gated SeedsResource wrapper. (g) Hand-author 2-3 reference 1v1 maps with zoned ore tiers. KILL-GATE the whole phase like Phase 0: playtest the five metrics; the two binary questions are "do my eyes stay on the battlefield?" and "is ignoring the civ layer still viable (~75% economy)?". PHASE 2 (CAMPAIGN, only after MATCHES validates): start with the Commander-only prototype (serialize one GainsExperience unit + 3-perk dossier across two stitched missions) to answer "development without homework"; the ~200-400 LOC CampaignState serializer + between-missions UI is the honest cost and a separate scoped task — do NOT block MATCHES on it. KEY FILES (all verified absolute): /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/rules/player.yaml (ResourceValues, untouched), /mods/ra/rules/vehicles.yaml:330 (HARV Capacity 20), /mods/ra/rules/civilian.yaml:518 (OILB template to inherit/reskin; also HOSP/FCOM/TECN), /mods/ra/rules/territory-economy.yaml (Phase-0 opt-in layer; re-point its supply-gating from 'the economy' to the ~20% bonus), /OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/CashTrickler.cs, /GivesBounty.cs, /Capturable.cs, /GainsExperience.cs, /Multipliers/ResourceValueMultiplier.cs, /Multipliers/ReloadDelayMultiplier.cs (copy-template for the new ChargeRateMultiplier), /SupportPowers/SupportPower.cs:21 (ChargeInterval — needs the new modifier hook), /Player/LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox.cs (the toggle), /Traits/Transforms.cs + /TransformOnCapture.cs (the develop verb), /Traits/World/SupplyNetwork.cs + /Traits/SupplyNode.cs (model the Foothold counter on these; deterministic integer/interval). THE ONE-LINE THESIS: keep the harvester loop sacred and at full strength; make territory a minority-cash, majority-capability AUGMENT whose economic structures AMPLIFY harvesting rather than print a parallel wallet; gate only a thin, map-anchored, capped, toggleable develop verb in matches; and reserve heavy persistence for a separately-scoped campaign built on the same machinery — every brake (diminishing returns, capturable-back, hard cap, ore-as-equalizer, attention-neutrality, the 0.75 ignorer floor) exists specifically to prevent the Phase-0 control-point failure from returning.

topConcerns: THE TRIANGLE COLLAPSES TO A LINE AT RA TEMPO. The pitch claims EXPAND/PROTECT/FIGHT all compete for the same attention 'fast and RA-paced' — but it then admits the entire triangle is manufactured by MAP DESIGN, not systems: safe-poor base ore, medium naturals, rich-contested center. That is just classic RA map design with extra labels. The honest test: in real RA the harvester loop and the army fight ALREADY co-exist because harvesting is near-zero-attention (autonomous Harvest activity). Layering 6-10 capturable structures on top doesn't add a third competing leg — it adds a SECOND combat objective (FIGHT-for-structures) that directly substitutes for FIGHT-for-army-kills. You don't get a triangle; you get the same EXPAND/PROTECT pair plus a control-point land-grab wearing a capability costume. The 'PROTECT harvesters' leg is the weakest corner in stock RA already (most players A-move and ignore harvester micro until raided); nothing here strengthens it except a GivesBounty trait that, I verified, is NOT on HARV in stock RA — so even that 'free, verified' raiding incentive is unbuilt mod-data.

CAPABILITY STRUCTURES ARE A BABYSITTING + LEGIBILITY TAX THAT PULLS THE CAMERA OFF THE FIGHT. The design's own kill-gate metric #4 is 'camera-time-on-army UP vs stock-RA-without-the-loop' — a rigged baseline.
