The real comparison is vs STOCK RA WITH the loop, and against that, 6-10 always-on capturable structures unambiguously ADD camera demands: each is a thing to scout, send an engineer/infantry to capture, garrison against recapture (OwnerLostAction=ChangeOwner means they flip the instant you look away), and re-take. RA is twitchy because there are FEW persistent map objectives. Capturable-back is sold as an anti-snowball virtue but it is simultaneously a perpetual babysitting generator: every one of 6-10 nodes is a standing recapture chore. That is the opposite of fast/readable. And the legibility problem the design flags in its own open questions is fatal at RA pace: 10 structures reskinning ~5 sprites (OILB/HOSP/FIX/DOME/FCOM/TECN) cannot be read apart in a 200-APM teamfight — you will misjudge which node does what, which is the single most un-RA failure mode.

THE AUGMENT/AMPLIFY ECONOMY IS INVISIBLE AND THEREFORE WON'T FEEL LIKE A REWARD — OR WILL QUIETLY DOMINATE. The flagship idea is loop-amplifiers (ResourceValueMultiplier +15-25% cash/ore, ProductionCostMultiplier -10-15%) instead of flat cash. The design itself flags this in open questions: amplifiers are INVISIBLE (no cash-tick feedback). A +20% ore multiplier produces zero dopamine, zero readable moment, and players will not feel they captured anything — which guts the whole 'develop the ground' fantasy. Worse for balance: a 60%-of-income ore spine getting +20% is a flat +12% total income that compounds with the bigger army it buys — that is a textbook snowball multiplier on the LARGEST income source, exactly what the four brakes are trying to prevent, smuggled in as the 'preferred' structure. You cannot simultaneously claim amplifiers are negligible-feeling AND that they meaningfully augment; one of those is false in playtest.

THE 0.75 IGNORER-FLOOR IS A NUMBER, NOT A GUARANTEE — AND THE MATH IS OPTIMISTIC. The non-negotiable bar is 'capture nothing, still field a full tech tree at ~75% economy.' But 75% economy in an RTS is not 75% strength — RTS economies compound, so a sustained 25% income deficit over a 15-20 min match is a losing position against an equal-skill opponent, not 'weaker but complete.' The design treats 0.75 as comfortable; against real opponents it is closer to the mandatory line than claimed. If playtest pushes the ignorer-floor up to feel fair, territory becomes pointless (their own alarm >0.90); if down, it becomes the control-point game they rejected. The viable band between 'pointless' and 'mandatory' for an additive compounding income source is narrow and the design has no evidence it exists — only a hope and a kill-gate.

THE MATCH CIV LAYER IS THREE SYSTEMS CALLED 'NOT A SYSTEM.' Develop-one-tier (Transforms) + a 0-100 Foothold meter with 2 thresholds + an irreversible Doctrine fork is, by any honest accounting, a system with state, thresholds, and a one-way strategic choice. The 'attention-neutral, set-and-forget' framing fights the fundamental truth the design itself states: 'optional dies the instant the optimal player MUST micro it.' A Foothold meter that grants self-repair at 50% and an extra build queue at 100% is NOT attention-neutral — an extra build queue is a permanent economic/military advantage that the optimal player will absolutely chase, which means contesting Foothold becomes mandatory, which means the toggle's 'develop-blind player wins 50/50' target fails. The design has already half-conceded this in its own Foothold open question ('need values that don't let the leader out-economy AND out-fight') — i.e., it does not yet have those values, and may not exist.
whatWouldFixIt: CUT THE TRIANGLE CLAIM DOWN TO A DUEL YOU CAN ACTUALLY DELIVER, AND PROVE PROTECT IS REAL FIRST. Before building any structures, do a zero-new-content playtest: stock RA + GivesBounty-on-HARV + 3 hand-zoned ore tiers. If harvester raiding doesn't become a live, camera-pulling lane on its own, the PROTECT leg is dead and no amount of capturable structures resurrects it — the triangle is a marketing line. Only proceed to structures if this micro-test alone already feels more RA-tense, not less.

SLASH THE STRUCTURE ROSTER TO 3-4 MAX FOR THE FIRST PROTOTYPE AND MAKE THEM SPRITE-DISTINCT. 10 reskins of 5 sprites is unreadable at RA pace — that's not a polish issue, it's a core-loop failure. Ship exactly: 1 Oil Derrick (flat legible cash, the dopamine anchor), 1 Repair Depot (FIX, universally useful so never a dead capture), 1 Radar/Detect node, 1 central Tech relic. Four nodes is enough to test 'does capturing pull my camera off the army too much?' without the legibility tax. Expand only if the 4-node version already feels RA-fast.

PREFER FLAT, VISIBLE CASH OVER INVISIBLE AMPLIFIERS FOR THE PROTOTYPE — INVERT THE STATED PREFERENCE. The design prefers amplifiers; do the opposite first. Flat CashTrickler at ~one-harvester's-income IS legible, gives the capture a felt reward, and is trivially balanceable/cappable. Reintroduce amplifiers only if flat cash playtests as 'too wallet-like' — and if you do, give them a VISIBLE tick (floating +cash on each amplified load) or they will feel like nothing and the develop fantasy dies.

DROP THE FOOTHOLD METER AND DOCTRINE FORK FROM PHASE 1 ENTIRELY. They are the parts most likely to violate attention-neutrality and most likely to be mandatory APM. Ship ONLY: always-on capturable structures + the lobby toggle gating a single one-time 'Develop this node' upgrade (Transforms). Test the two binary questions ('eyes stay on battlefield?' / 'ignoring it ~75% viable?') against THAT minimal layer. If a single develop-click already drifts toward mandatory, the meter+doctrine would have been catastrophic — and you've saved building them.

FIX THE RIGGED KILL-GATE BASELINE. Metric #4 must compare camera-time-on-army against STOCK RA WITH the harvester loop (the real game), not against a strawman stock-RA-without-the-loop. If THEATER pulls the camera off the army more than real RA does, it has failed the lens regardless of what the other metrics say. Make that the primary gate; the economy ratios are secondary.

RE-DERIVE THE IGNORER FLOOR FROM WIN-RATE, NOT INCOME RATIO. 0.75 income is the wrong target because income compounds. Set the gate as: a capture-nothing player of equal skill wins >=~45% vs a full-territory player. If they can't, the floor is too low whatever the income ratio says. This is the only honest version of 'territory is an edge you fight for, not a tax you pay to not lose.'
critiques.detail: I verified the load-bearing facts: ore is Ore 25/Gems 50 (mods/ra/rules/player.yaml), HARV Capacity 20 (vehicles.yaml:330), OILB CashTrickler is Amount 100 / Interval 375 (civilian.yaml:542-544), CashTrickler defaults Amount 15 / Interval 50 (CashTrickler.cs:22-28), ChargeInterval is a readonly field with no modifier hook (SupportPower.cs:21). Those numbers are solid. Two claims are oversold as 'verified stock': (1) GivesBounty is NOT present on HARV in stock RA (grep found nothing in vehicles.yaml) — harvester raiding being 'free via verified stock GivesBounty' is unbuilt mod-data, and it is the ONLY thing making the PROTECT leg of the triangle real, so this matters. (2) SupplyNode.cs / SupplyNetwork.cs / territory-economy.yaml exist in the tree but are Phase-0 prototype artifacts, not stock OpenRA primitives — fine to reuse, but they're your own untested code, not battle-proven engine.\n\nThe corrected thesis (augment, don't replace; keep ore stock; minority-cash/majority-capability) is genuinely the right correction to the Phase-0 failure, and the discipline around anti-snowball brakes, one-wallet, and progressive disclosure is real and rare. That's why this is fun-with-fixes, not risky. But as a pace purist I have to name what the prose is hiding from itself: the triangle is asserted as a NEW third leg of competing attention when it is mechanically the OLD expand/protect pair plus a second combat objective (capturing/holding structures) that substitutes for army combat rather than adding a distinct axis. RA's twitch comes precisely from FEW persistent map objectives and a near-autonomous harvester loop; 6-10 always-on capturable nodes with ChangeOwner-on-loss are a standing recapture/babysitting generator and a legibility tax (10 nodes, ~5 reskinned sprites) that pull the camera off the army — the exact thing the lens exists to protect. The Foothold meter granting an extra build queue, and the +20% ore amplifier compounding on the largest income source, are the two places where 'attention-neutral, anti-snowball' quietly becomes 'mandatory and snowbally,' and the design's own open questions already concede it does not yet have safe values for either. Strip Phase 1 to 4 distinct structures + flat visible cash + one develop-click + the toggle, kill the meter/doctrine until that minimum passes a camera-time gate measured against REAL RA, and prove the PROTECT leg with a bounty-only micro-test before building anything. Does it still feel like Red Alert? At the 4-node/flat-cash/no-meter floor, plausibly yes. At the full 10-node/amplifier/Foothold/Doctrine spec, my honest read is no — it feels like a control-point RTS with an RA skin, which is the exact failure you already rejected once.

critiques.lens: Complexity-trap / engagement — trying to prove THEATER sneaks the Stellaris/Civ engagement-killers back in, that "light" creeps, that the toggle forks the game, and that campaign persistence becomes a chore/snowball/death-spiral.
topConcerns: TECHNICAL FALSEHOOD AT THE THESIS'S CORE: The 'amplify-don't-duplicate' pillar — the structural mechanism that supposedly welds territory to the harvester loop — does NOT work as the claimed mod-data. Verified: IResourceValueModifier is consumed at Refinery.cs:52 via self.TraitsImplementing<IResourceValueModifier>() — read off the REFINERY ACTOR, never the player. A captured 'Refinery Concession' granting a player-scoped ResourceValueMultiplier amplifies NOTHING; the multiplier only applies to the actor it physically sits on. The design names this as the preferred economic structure (the one that pays zero if you stop harvesting) and lists it as mod-data + 'only two new C# traits.' That is false. Making it player-wide requires NEW C# in the refinery's value path. The keystone of the corrected thesis is currently vaporware, and the design doesn't know it.

THE TOGGLE CREATES THE TWO-MODES PROBLEM IT CLAIMS TO DODGE — by ranked-locking the one mode with depth. 'LOCKED OFF in ranked 1v1, DEFAULT ON in skirmish/co-op.' This means the develop layer — the entire 'civ' pitch, the reason this isn't just RA — is NEVER balanced against a thinking human opponent. It only ever runs vs AI and in unranked customs. The competitive surface that gets iterated, watched, and discussed is byte-identical RA. The depth layer becomes a single-player toy that the strongest players never touch and the balance team never tunes. That is not 'RA-plus-a-bit'; it's 'RA, plus an unbalanced sandbox no one is accountable for.' The toggle doesn't fork the community — it orphans the new content.

'LIGHT' IS ALREADY CREEPING — the match layer is not 3 things, it's a system pretending to be 3 things. Count the actual cognitive surface a competent player must model: 6-10 capturable structures (10 verbs to read at RA pace, all reskinning ~5 sprites — the design's own openQuestion #9 admits legibility may force cutting the roster), + per-player diminishing-returns brackets on cash nodes (14/12/10/6) that change on every capture/recapture, + a Foothold meter with 2 thresholds, + a Develop verb with cost-vs-army tradeoffs, + an irreversible Doctrine fork. The '3-4 decisions' framing counts only the develop CLICKS while hiding the CONTINUOUS valuation load (which node is worth which, who's near which bracket, is my opponent about to cross 50%). That valuation load IS the Civ/Stellaris tax — it doesn't show up as menu time, it shows up as attention you can't spend on micro. The brake count itself (FOUR anti-snowball mechanisms stacked on territory cash) is the tell: a mechanic needing four simultaneous governors to not break is not 'light.'

ATTENTION-NEUTRALITY IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY AND THEREFORE UNACHIEVABLE. The kill-gate demands a develop-blind player beats a develop-heavy player ~50/50. But the design ALSO wants develop to be 'an interesting choice' (develop the node OR build two tanks) and the Foothold thresholds to feel 'game-defining.' These are mutually exclusive: if ignoring the layer is genuinely ~50/50 viable, the layer is by definition decorative and the 'civ depth' pitch is dead; if the layer is game-defining, ignoring it loses and APM-neutrality fails. The design has written a pass/fail gate that one half of its own goals must fail. You cannot have a meaningful develop verb that is also free to ignore.

CAMPAIGN PERSISTENCE STILL SNOWBALLS THROUGH THE VETERAN CADRE despite the brakes. The 'reset capital, persist capability' law is clean in theory, but a 3-6 unit veteran cadre returning as pre-leveled reinforcements every mission IS persistent combat power that compounds — verified GainsExperience gives real stat/ability jumps. Against the design's own 'difficulty scales with progress, not player strength' rule, you get the WC3/XCOM oscillation: either the cadre trivializes missions (snowball) or the difficulty-scaling negates the cadre's value (why did I protect them?). 'Downed-not-dead' + guaranteed-floor softens the death-spiral but guarantees the cadre rarely matters — turning the emotional centerpiece (the survivors you extracted) into a stat-stick the difficulty curve quietly cancels. The emotion and the balance are at war.

CAMPAIGN IS A NET-NEW PERSISTENCE ENGINE, not 'the same machinery, just serialized.' Verified: zero campaign state carry-over exists in the engine; missions are stateless chains. The design admits ~200-400 LOC, but undersells it: a serialized CampaignState re-injected as pre-game inits on ALL clients identically for co-op is a determinism-critical, save-versioning, migration-on-update surface — the exact class of system that rots. Calling it 'a separate scoped task' is correct triage but the campaign is sold as the 'deeper secondary mode' that justifies the whole civ framing; if it's deferred and risky, the project's emotional payoff is the part most likely to never ship.
whatWouldFixIt: FIX THE AMPLIFIER LIE FIRST, before any YAML. Either (a) accept the amplifier needs new C#: add a player-level IResourceValueModifier query to Refinery's value calc (small, but it IS engine work — update the design's 'two new traits' to three and stop calling the amplifier mod-data), or (b) drop the player-scoped amplifier entirely and make the economic structures flat CashTrickler derricks (which DO work as mod-data) — and then honestly admit territory is a second wallet and lean on diminishing-returns + the ore-equalizer to keep it from being a control-point game. Pick one. The current design rests on a mechanism that compiles to nothing.

RESOLVE THE TOGGLE FORK BY BALANCING THE DEEP MODE, NOT HIDING IT. If develop is the product, ranked 1v1 must be develop-ON (one canonical surface WITH the layer), or you must accept develop is single-player-only flavor and stop pitching it as the competitive identity. The worst outcome — locked-off-in-ranked, default-on-everywhere-else — guarantees the new content is never balanced. Choose: it's competitive (balance it in ranked) or it's a sandbox (say so, and right-size the ambition).

REPLACE THE ~50/50 ATTENTION-NEUTRALITY GATE with an honest target like 52-55/45-48 to the engaged player, and explicitly state 'the develop layer is a real edge, not free.' Then the gate becomes achievable and the depth pitch survives. Keep the HARD ceiling (develop-heavy must not exceed ~60% / mandatory-APM) but stop pretending ignoring it is free — that was always a contradiction.

HARD-CUT THE STRUCTURE ROSTER TO 4-5 DISTINCT TYPES for the first prototype (1 derrick, 1 repair, 1 radar, 1 tech relic, 1 forward-command), one sprite-reskin each, and prove legibility at RA pace BEFORE adding the other five. The design's own openQuestion #9 already fears this; act on the fear. Ten verbs reskinning five sprites is the legibility failure the user will hit in the first playtest.

CAP CADRE IMPACT EXPLICITLY: make veteran cadre a SIDEGRADE/identity (unlock an ability, a unique unit) rather than raw stat compounding, so 'I protected them' pays in flavor/options not power — matching the dossier philosophy. This dissolves the snowball-vs-pointless oscillation: the difficulty curve can't cancel a sidegrade the way it cancels a stat-stick.

BUILD THE COMMANDER-ONLY PROTOTYPE THE DESIGN ALREADY PROPOSES, and gate the entire campaign investment on it answering 'development without homework' YES — but add a second gate: 'does the difficulty-scaling make persistence feel meaningful or cancelled?' If persistence and anti-snowball can't both feel good in the 2-mission stitch, the campaign's core promise is unsound and should be re-scoped before the 200-400 LOC serializer is written.
critiques.detail:
VERDICT RATIONALE — fun-with-fixes, leaning risky on two specific points. This design is dramatically better than the rejected Phase-0 (ore->0 was a genuine fun-killer; keeping ore stock at Ore 25/Gems 50 and HARV capacity 20 — both verified in player.yaml and vehicles.yaml — preserves the sacred loop, which is the single most important correct call here). The instinct to make territory AUGMENT not REPLACE is right, and most of the trait substrate is real: I verified Capturable, CashTrickler, GivesBounty, GainsExperience, LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox, ResourceValueMultiplier, ProductionCostMultiplier, and SupportPower.ChargeInterval (line 21, a plain int field with no modifier interface — the design's 'needs new C#' claim is accurate). SupplyNetwork.cs is integer/interval/[Sync]-shaped as claimed. The honesty about the campaign-persistence gap (verified: no carry-over exists, missions are stateless) is genuinely good engineering discipline.

BUT the review brief asks whether the civ layer SNEAKS IN the engagement-killers, and on three counts it does:

1. THE THESIS-KEYSTONE IS TECHNICALLY BROKEN. The 'amplify-don't-duplicate' pillar is the structural argument that this isn't a second-wallet control-point game. I verified it doesn't work: IResourceValueModifier is consumed at Refinery.cs:52 off the refinery actor, not the player. The flagship 'Refinery Concession' amplifier is mod-data that amplifies nothing. The design's central anti-trap mechanism is, as written, non-functional — and the design believes it's free mod-data. This is the most serious finding because the whole 'we avoid the control-point failure' argument leans on it.

2. THE TOGGLE ORPHANS THE DEPTH. Locked-off-in-ranked + default-on-elsewhere means the entire civ layer is never balanced against humans. The 'does the toggle fork the community' question is answered by quietly conceding the deep mode isn't competitive — which guts the pitch.

3. 'LIGHT' IS A COUNTING TRICK. The '3-4 decisions' figure counts develop-clicks while hiding the continuous valuation load (10 structures, shifting diminishing-return brackets, opponent's Foothold proximity). That hidden valuation load is exactly the Stellaris tax, just relocated from menu-time to attention-you-can't-micro-with. Four stacked anti-snowball brakes on one cash stream is itself evidence the mechanic is heavier than 'light.'

The attention-neutrality kill-gate is internally contradictory (can't be both ignorable ~50/50 AND a meaningful interesting-choice). The campaign's veteran cadre re-creates the snowball-vs-pointless oscillation the difficulty-scaling rule is supposed to prevent, putting emotion and balance at war.

None of these are fatal — they're fixable, and the kill-gate-everything methodology is exactly the discipline that will catch them in playtest. But the design currently OVERSTATES its own safety: it presents a broken mechanism as working, an unbalanced mode as 'RA-plus-a-bit,' and a contradictory gate as a clean pass/fail. Fix the amplifier-C# reality, pick a side on the toggle, cut the roster to 5, and re-scope the cadre as sidegrade-not-statstick, and this crosses into 'fun.' Ship the MATCHES phase first as planned; do NOT write the campaign serializer until the Commander-only prototype proves persistence and difficulty-scaling can BOTH feel good simultaneously.

topConcerns: THE AMPLIFIER THESIS IS BROKEN AGAINST THE STOCK ENGINE. The design's structural cornerstone — the 'Refinery Concession' that routes territory value THROUGH the harvester loop via ResourceValueMultiplier — does not work as a captured map structure. Verified at OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildings/Refinery.cs:52: IResourceValueModifier is queried with self.TraitsImplementing<>() on the REFINERY actor, not the player. A captured node on the map cannot grant a player-scoped cash-per-ore boost with stock traits. Worse, resourceValueModifiers is cached ONCE in Created() (line 52, INotifyCreated) and never refreshed — so even if you bolted the multiplier onto each refinery, capturing or losing the Concession mid-match would NOT change anyone's income. The 'pays zero if you stop harvesting / dynamic amplifier that welds territory to the spine' is the single most-repeated claim in the doc (AMPLIFY-DON'T-DUPLICATE guard, economySplit, territoryStructures) and it requires NEW C# the doc lists as mod-data. The whole anti-second-wallet defense leans on a mechanism that isn't real yet.

THE 20%-TERRITORY-CASH CEILING COLLAPSES UNDER ITS OWN STARTING NUMBERS. Doc's kill-gate (3) alarms if territory-cash creeps past ~20% of total. But with the doc's own numbers — DR cash nodes 14/12/10/6 = 42 cr/s at 4 nodes, vs a harvester loop at ~18-20 cr/s/harvester (HARV Capacity 20 x Ore 25 = 500cr/load) — a player with 4 harvesters and 4 cash nodes is at 42/(72+42) = ~37% territory cash, nearly DOUBLE the ceiling. The 60/40 (of which only 20 cash) target only holds if players field 8+ harvesters per cash node. Early game, when fights are decided, harvester counts are 2-4, so territory cash is 40-55% of income — squarely the rejected control-point economy. The ratio doesn't 'collapse to a dominant line' later; it's inverted EARLIEST, exactly when snowball matters most.

FLAT CASH DERRICKS ARE A MUST-GRAB AND THE DR BRAKE IS A LOCKSTEP LIABILITY. The roster keeps OILB-style flat CashTrickler nodes 'for nostalgia/tempo' (8-14 cr/s, no harvesting required). Unlike the amplifiers, these print free money decoupled from the loop — so they ARE the second wallet the user rejected, just smaller. They will be the first capture every game, every map, because cash with zero opportunity cost dominates capability whose value is matchup-dependent (the doc's own open question admits Radar/Repair can be 'a dead capture'). The diminishing-returns brake (14/12/10/6) requires a per-player held-node-count that re-evaluates a granted condition on EVERY capture and recapture — a real synced surface the doc flags in openQuestions but treats as solved. Rapid recapture trades over a contested node are precisely where stepped-bracket condition recompute can desync if not carefully ordered.

THE TOGGLE DOESN'T FORK BALANCE, BUT IT FORKS THE PLAYERBASE'S SKILL TRANSFER. The claim that OFF is 'byte-identical map/structure/capture game' is structurally true and the strongest part of the design. But locking the develop layer OFF in ranked 1v1 while defaulting it ON in skirmish/co-op means the mode where players LEARN (vs AI) trains a different optimal than the mode where they're RANKED. The capability structures are always-on in both, so a skirmish player internalizes 'develop the node + Foothold thresholds' as correct play, then ranked strips it. This is the SC2 co-op-vs-1v1 split the doc cites as a positive, but here it cuts against onboarding rather than for it.

MULTIPLAYER HEALTH: THE TRIANGLE'S ANTI-SNOWBALL CLAIM ('out-expander fields more exposed harvesters, so aggression scales with greed') is asserted but the structures cut the other way. A territory leader holding the central rich-ore + co-located Repair Depot + Radar + Tech Center gets vision over the routes, forward repair for the defending army, and faster support-power charge — i.e. the capability nodes make the leader BETTER at protecting the very harvesters the comeback lane depends on raiding. The 'ore-as-equalizer' comeback assumes the behind player can reach those exposed routes, but the contested center co-locates economy AND the vision/detection that denies raids. The design stacks the anti-snowball brake (raidable harvesters) and the snowball accelerant (vision/repair/charge over the same ground) on the SAME tile, and there's no evidence the brake wins.
whatWouldFixIt: Make the amplifier real and player-scoped BEFORE relying on it as the anti-second-wallet defense. This needs new C#, not mod-data: either (a) a new IResourceValueModifier that lives on the PlayerActor and a change to Refinery.cs to query self.Owner.PlayerActor.TraitsImplementing<>() AND to recompute the modifier list on a condition-change/owner-change notify instead of caching it once in Created(); or (b) a per-player ResourceValueMultiplier driven by GrantConditionOnPrerequisite from the captured node, with Refinery re-resolving modifiers each AcceptResources call. Until this exists, demote the amplifier thesis from 'cornerstone' to 'aspirational' and don't let the design's balance story depend on it.

Re-derive the cash-node numbers from a realistic EARLY-GAME harvester count (2-4), not a saturated late-game one. Set total territory-cash as a HARD percentage of the player's actual ore income (a player-level cap trait), not a flat cr/s schedule — flat schedules invert the ratio whenever harvester count is low. Target: territory cash auto-throttles so it can never exceed ~25% of THIS player's current ore rate, measured live.

Cut or radically de-emphasize flat-cash derricks. Every cash node should be an amplifier (zero value if not harvesting) or carry a steep opportunity cost. If you keep one flat derrick 'for nostalgia,' make it a single, central, contested relic (AoE2-relic rule the doc already cites) — never 2-4 scattered free-money nodes, which guarantee a must-grab opening and the second-wallet feel.

Prototype the diminishing-returns condition as discrete integer brackets and write a determinism/replay test that hammers rapid recapture trades over one node specifically, before trusting it. Decide per-player-global (simpler, safer) over per-structure. Treat this as a sim-touching change requiring the same kill-gate as ChargeInterval.

Decouple the snowball accelerants from the comeback ground. Do NOT co-locate Radar/Repair/Tech-Center with the richest contested ore on the same tiles — that lets the leader's capability deny the exact raids the comeback lane needs. Put detection/vision capability AWAY from the leader's economy, or give every capability node a small universal baseline (the doc's own open question) so capturing-back is meaningful and no node is a dead grab that only the leader benefits from holding.

Resolve the onboarding fork: either default the develop layer OFF in skirmish-vs-AI too (so the learning surface matches ranked), or commit to a ranked ladder that includes it. Training players on a superset of ranked rules is the inverted version of the SC2 lesson the doc cites approvingly.

Add an explicit early-game snowball kill-gate, not just the minute-8 win% one. Measure win% of the FIRST-cash-node capturer at minute 3-4; if grabbing the opening derrick predicts the win >55%, the territory economy is front-loaded into a control-point game regardless of the late-game ratio.
critiques.detail:
The corrected thesis (territory AUGMENTS, ore stays sacred) is genuinely the right correction to the Phase-0 failure, and the toggle's structural separation (OFF = byte-identical capture game) is a real, defensible answer to the 'forks the community' risk — that part is sound and I couldn't break it. The design is also admirably honest in its openQuestions. My adversarial job is the gap between the doc's confident balance prose and what the engine actually does, and that gap is load-bearing.

The central problem: the design's entire defense against re-creating the rejected control-point game rests on the AMPLIFY-DON'T-DUPLICATE principle — economic structures whose value is zero if you stop harvesting, structurally welding territory to the ore spine. I verified this mechanism does not exist against stock traits. Refinery.cs:52 queries IResourceValueModifier on the refinery actor (not the player) and caches the result once at construction (INotifyCreated.Created), never refreshing on capture/loss. So a captured map structure cannot grant the player-scoped, dynamic, capture-sensitive cash-per-ore boost the doc describes in three separate sections. It needs new C# the doc miscategorizes as mod-data. Strip the broken amplifiers and what remains are flat CashTrickler derricks — which ARE the decoupled second wallet the user rejected, just smaller and dressed in diminishing returns.

The numbers compound this. The doc's own starting values (DR nodes 14/12/10/6 = 42 cr/s at 4 nodes; harvester ~18-20 cr/s from the verified HARV Capacity 20 x Ore 25 = 500/load) put territory cash at ~37% of total with 4 harvesters — and far higher (40-55%) at the 2-4 harvester counts that actually exist when early fights decide the game. The 20%-cash ceiling the design treats as a guardrail is violated by its own opening numbers. The split doesn't 'collapse to a dominant economic line' over time; it's inverted at minute 3, which is worse, because that's when the snowball seed is planted.

Verified facts used: mods/ra/rules/player.yaml (Ore 25/Gems 50, unchanged — good, thesis-consistent); vehicles.yaml:330 (HARV Capacity 20); civilian.yaml:542 (OILB CashTrickler Interval 375 / Amount 100 = 6.67 cr/s at Timestep 40 = 25tps); territory-economy.yaml confirmed as the opt-in Phase-0 file that zeroes ore (correctly NOT in mod.yaml); CashTrickler.cs (Amount/Interval are flat readonly ints, no native per-player node-count scaling — the DR brake is all new condition plumbing); ResourceValueMultiplier.cs + Refinery.cs:52,60 (refinery-scoped, cached); SupportPower.cs:21 (ChargeInterval plain readonly int, confirms the one admitted new sim hook). The diminishing-returns brake and the ChargeRateMultiplier are both genuine lockstep surfaces that the doc under-weights as 'mod-data' or '~40 lines.'

Verdict is fun-with-fixes, not risky, because the skeleton is salvageable and the toggle architecture is solid: the ore loop stays sacred, the capture game is additive, and the kill-gate discipline is the right instinct. But three things must be true before a playtest means anything — (1) the amplifier must actually be built and player-scoped, (2) the cash schedule must be re-derived from early-game harvester counts and capped as a live percentage of the player's own ore rate rather than a flat cr/s, and (3) the snowball accelerants (vision/repair/charge) must not sit on the same tiles as the comeback ore. Until then the design will playtest as a smaller, better-dressed version of the exact control-point game the user already rejected — and the doc's own metric (3) will trip on turn one.

topConcerns: THE AMPLIFIER THESIS HAS A HOLE AT THE ENGINE LEVEL. The entire 'weld territory to the ore loop' argument rests on ResourceValueMultiplier being player-scoped. It is not. /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildings/Refinery.cs:52 reads resourceValueModifiers from self.TraitsImplementing<IResourceValueModifier>() ONCE in INotifyCreated.Created and caches the array for the refinery's lifetime. The interface lives on the refinery actor, not the player. So a captured 'Refinery Concession' cannot raise cash-per-ore via stock ResourceValueMultiplier: (a) the modifier must live on each Refinery, not on a captured tech building; (b) it is cached at refinery construction, so capturing the structure mid-match grants nothing to refineries that already exist, and loses nothing when recaptured. The design's flagship non-cash 'amplifier' (the structure that supposedly pays zero if you stop harvesting) is NOT mod-data and NOT a 40-line trait — it requires NEW C#: either an owner-scoped/player-level resource-value modifier that Refinery re-queries each delivery (touching the hot delivery path and re-reading the cache), or a per-refinery condition propagated on capture. This is the corrected-thesis cornerstone and it is mislabeled as free.

DIMINISHING-RETURNS-ON-CAPTURE IS MORE C# THAN ADMITTED. The anti-snowball brake (14/12/10/6 cr/sec by held-cash-node count) requires a per-player count of held cash-nodes that re-evaluates on every capture/loss and re-grants a stepped CashTrickler rate. Stock CashTrickler has no 'rate depends on how many siblings my owner holds' input. There is no stock trait that counts owner-held actors-of-a-class and feeds a bracket. This is a new player-scoped counter trait + condition plumbing — the design's own openQuestion #2 admits the lockstep concern but the sequencing plan files it under 'stock CashTrickler.' At least 3 of the load-bearing economic mechanisms (amplifier, diminishing returns, hard-cap-at-20%) are net-new C#, not the claimed two traits.

TWO 'NEW C#' TRAITS ARE REAL BUT ONE IS UNDERSPECIFIED AND ONE IS A DETERMINISM TRAP. Verified: SupportPower.cs:21 ChargeInterval has no modifier interface (correct — new ISupportPowerChargeModifier needed). And SeedsResource.cs:55 uses Util.RandomWalk(self.Location, self.World.SharedRandom) — SharedRandom IS the deterministic MersenneTwister (World.cs:199), so seeding is sync-safe AS STOCK. But the design wants a 'gated/owner-scoped SeedsResource wrapper' for a Prospecting Station; any owner-scoping that branches on per-player state inside the seed path risks pulling SharedRandom out of identical-call-order across clients. The charge-rate modifier touches the support-power charge tick, the single most replay-sensitive subsystem. Neither is hard, but neither is the trivial 'mirror ReloadDelayMultiplier' the design implies — both need a dedicated replay/desync test before trust.

CAMPAIGN PERSISTENCE COST IS HONESTLY FLAGGED BUT STILL UNDER-PRICED, AND IT IS THE SECONDARY MODE. Verified the statelessness claim is true: missions.yaml is a bare ordered list of map names (mods/ra/missions.yaml), and GameSave.cs is a within-match order/sync-packet stream (Network/GameSave.cs:84-89), NOT cross-mission state. So persistence genuinely needs new C#. But '200-400 LOC + thin UI' ignores: the between-missions UI is a whole new screen/flow (no precedent in this codebase), co-op CampaignState-load determinism is unsolved (the design admits this), save-file versioning/migration as the dossier schema evolves, and the four-pillar serialization surface (hero level+wargear, cadre roster, dossier, home-theater nodes) is itself a mini data model. Realistic floor is closer to 600-1000 LOC + UI + save-migration discipline — for the SECONDARY mode. The recommendation to defer it is correct; the cost estimate that makes deferral feel cheap is optimistic.

STRUCTURE LEGIBILITY IS A REAL SHIP-BLOCKER THE DESIGN ITSELF HALF-CONCEDES. 10 capturable structures reskinning ~5-6 RA sprites (OILB/HOSP/FIX/DOME/FCOM/TECN) at RA pace, distinguished only by tooltip + banner, in the same fights where the player is also microing harvesters and army. The design's own openQuestion #9 admits this may force cutting the roster. At RA's twitch tempo a player will not read 'is that the Refinery Concession or the Foundry' off two near-identical reskinned sprites mid-fight — which silently kills the heterogeneity-is-the-point thesis because players treat all structures as 'capture point, get something.'
whatWouldFixIt: FIX THE AMPLIFIER AT THE SOURCE OR DROP IT FROM PHASE 0b. Either (a) accept that the cash-per-ore amplifier needs a new player-scoped IResourceValueModifier that Refinery re-queries on every AcceptResources call (not cached in Created) — scope it explicitly as the FIRST new-C# task, ~1-2 days incl. replay test, not a free reskin; or (b) for the cheapest hybrid-thesis test, drop the amplifier entirely from the first playtest and prove the thesis with the OUTPUT-side ProductionCostMultiplier instead, which IS genuinely a stock per-producer trait gated by a captured-structure prerequisite. Re-label the design: 'amplifiers' are net-new sim C#, 'cost discounts' are mod-data.

SMALLEST PHASE 0b (this is the whole answer to the cheap-test question): ZERO new C#, ONE map, ONE binary question. Author mods/ra/rules/theater.yaml with TWO capturable structures only — one Oil Derrick (stock CashTrickler ~10 cr/sec) and one Repair Depot (stock RepairsUnits) — on a single hand-zoned 1v1 map with stock ore (Ore 25/Gems 50, already correct in player.yaml:5-6). NO toggle, NO Foothold meter, NO Develop verb, NO doctrines, NO diminishing-returns trait, NO new C#. Playtest exactly two kill-gates: (1) does ignoring both structures still leave you at ~0.75 economy and a complete tech tree? (2) do your eyes stay on the harvester loop? This tests the corrected hybrid thesis ('territory augments, doesn't replace') for the price of one YAML file and one map — and crucially proves whether ONE cash node + ONE capability node already creates the EXPAND/PROTECT/FIGHT triangle before any layer is built.

CUT FOR PHASE 0b/1, in priority order: (1) the Foothold meter (it's the SupplyNetwork-modeled world trait + thresholds + condition plumbing — defer until the base capture game is proven fun); (2) the Doctrine pick (irreversible fork with no replay data behind it — openQuestion #5 already doubts it); (3) the one-tier Develop verb (Transforms-based but needs a new IResolveOrder order + banner art + UI affordance); (4) the diminishing-returns trait (replace with a simple HARD CAP via fewer cash nodes on the map — 2 cash nodes max — which needs zero code); (5) the Prospecting Station SeedsResource wrapper and the SupportPower charge modifier (both new sim C#, both replay-risky, neither tests the core thesis). The lobby toggle (LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox, verified present) only matters once there's a layer to gate — defer it with the layer.

DECIDE STRUCTURE LEGIBILITY EMPIRICALLY AND EARLY: cap the first roster at 3-4 structure TYPES with maximally different silhouettes/functions (cash, repair, vision, buildable-area), give each a hard-readable banner color, and add the rest only if playtesters can name a captured structure at a glance during a fight. Treat 'players can't tell them apart at RA pace' as a kill-gate, not a polish item — it directly determines whether heterogeneity survives.

RE-SEQUENCE THE HONEST-COST LINE: state plainly that the hybrid MATCH economy needs ~3 net-new player-scoped sim traits (re-querying resource modifier, held-node counter for diminishing returns / or just cap via map, support-power charge modifier) PLUS the campaign serializer (~600-1000 LOC + UI + save-migration) for the secondary mode. The campaign is worth it ONLY after the Commander-only prototype (one GainsExperience unit serialized across two stitched skirmishes) answers 'development without homework' — keep that gate, but price it honestly so a 'no' there saves the larger cost.
critiques.detail:
Verified against the live repo. Stock ore values are correct (player.yaml:5-6 Ore 25/Gems 50). The named stock traits all exist (CashTrickler, GivesBounty, Capturable, GainsExperience, GivesCashOnCapture, RevealsShroud, RepairsUnits, DetectCloaked, GivesBuildableArea, Transforms, TransformOnCapture, LobbyPrerequisiteCheckbox, the full Multipliers/ folder). SupplyNetwork.cs and SupplyNode.cs exist. The campaign-statelessness claim is accurate (missions.yaml is a bare map-name list; GameSave.cs is a within-match order/sync stream). So the design's homework is largely real — this is NOT a fantasy build.

But the lens is 'engine reality,' and the design's central economic mechanism does not survive contact with the engine as written. ResourceValueMultiplier (the flagship 'amplifier' that supposedly welds territory to the harvester loop and pays zero if you stop harvesting) is consumed in Refinery.cs:52 via self.TraitsImplementing<IResourceValueModifier>(), cached once in INotifyCreated.Created, scoped to the refinery actor, never re-read. A captured tech building cannot grant it; capturing it mid-match changes nothing for existing refineries; recapturing it costs nothing. The corrected thesis's structural enforcement ('amplifiers route value THROUGH the loop') is the one piece the design most needs to be free, and it is the one piece that is genuinely new sim C#. The diminishing-returns brake has the same problem — no stock trait counts owner-held nodes and feeds a stepped rate. So the 'only two new ~40-line traits' claim undercounts by roughly 3 economic mechanisms.

The verdict is fun-with-fixes, not risky, for one reason: the SMALLEST honest test of the hybrid thesis needs none of that. One YAML file, one map, one stock cash node + one stock capability node, stock ore. That configuration tests the only question that actually killed Phase-0 ('does ignoring territory still leave a complete economy / do my eyes stay on the loop') without building the amplifier, the meter, the doctrines, the develop verb, the toggle, or any new C# at all. If that 2-structure map is fun, the thesis is validated and the team earns the right to build the expensive layer. If it isn't, the whole edifice was going to fail and the team learned it for the cost of an afternoon. Everything heavier — the Foothold meter, doctrines, develop verb, diminishing-returns trait, charge modifier, prospecting station, and the entire campaign persistence stack — should be deferred behind that gate. The campaign in particular is the secondary mode carrying the largest and most under-priced cost (a new save subsystem, a new between-missions screen, unsolved co-op determinism, and save-migration discipline); deferring it is correct, but the team should price it at 600-1000 LOC + UI, not 200-400, so a 'no' at the Commander-only prototype actually saves that money.

Key files for the fixes: /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildings/Refinery.cs:45-60 (the cached, actor-scoped resource modifier — the amplifier blocker), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Multipliers/ResourceValueMultiplier.cs (per-actor as written), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/TraitsInterfaces.cs:488 (IResourceValueModifier), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/SupportPowers/SupportPower.cs:21 (ChargeInterval, no modifier — new hook correctly identified), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/SeedsResource.cs:55 (uses World.SharedRandom — deterministic as stock, but owner-scoped branching is the risk), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/missions.yaml (bare list, confirms statelessness), /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Game/Network/GameSave.cs:84-89 (within-match orders, not cross-mission state).

verdict.overallVerdict: CONDITIONAL GREEN, scoped way down. The corrected hybrid thesis is right and worth building, but NOT at the spec'd size. Ship a 2-structure, zero-new-C#, single-map Phase 0b first; defer everything else behind it.
verdict.rationale:
Synthesizing the four lenses (not averaging): all four independently land on "fun-with-fixes," and three of them independently verified the SAME load-bearing failure — so this is not four soft opinions, it's one hard convergent finding plus a strong shared correction. I confirmed both directly in the repo: (1) the amplifier keystone is broken. Refinery.cs:51 caches resourceValueModifiers ONCE in INotifyCreated.Created from self.TraitsImplementing<IResourceValueModifier>() (refinery-actor scope), and AcceptResources reuses that cached array. So a captured, player-scoped "Refinery Concession" amplifies nothing, and capturing/losing it mid-match changes income for zero existing refineries. The design's central anti-"second-wallet" mechanism — "amplifiers route value THROUGH the loop and pay zero if you stop harvesting" — does not exist as mod-data and is mislabeled as such across three sections. (2) GivesBounty is NOT on HARV in stock RA; the "PROTECT harvesters" leg of the triangle — the only leg that strengthens the thing the user loves — is unbuilt mod-data, not "free/verified." Ore is correctly stock (25/50). 

Why CONDITIONAL GREEN and not RED: the thesis is genuinely the correct fix to the Phase-0 failure (the user already proved ore->0 kills the fun; keeping ore sacred is the single most important right call here), and crucially the SMALLEST honest test of that thesis needs none of the broken or heavy machinery. The scope/engine lens nails it: one cash node + one capability node + stock ore on one hand-zoned map tests the only question that actually killed Phase-0 ("does ignoring territory still leave a complete economy, and do my eyes stay on the loop") for the price of one YAML file. If that 2-node map is fun, the team earns the expensive layer. If not, the whole edifice was going to fail and they learned it in an afternoon.

Why NOT a clean GREEN on the full design: the spec OVERSTATES its own safety in three measurable ways. (a) The math inverts its own guardrail: DR cash nodes at 14/12/10/6 = 42 cr/s against a harvester at ~18-20 cr/s puts territory cash at ~37% with 4 harvesters and 40-55% at the 2-4 harvester counts that actually decide early fights — double-to-triple the design's own 20% ceiling, and front-loaded into exactly the snowball window. The 0.75 ignorer-floor is also an income ratio, and income compounds, so 0.75 income is well below 0.75 strength over a 15-20 min match — the honest gate is win-rate, not income. (b) Attention-neutrality is internally contradictory: a layer cannot be both ~50/50-ignorable AND a "game-defining" interesting choice (an extra build queue at Foothold 100% is a permanent advantage the optimal player WILL chase). (c) The toggle as specced (locked-OFF ranked, default-ON elsewhere) orphans the depth layer — it is then never balanced against a human and never learned in the mode that's ranked. None of these are fatal, but they mean the full 10-structure/amplifier/Foothold/Doctrine build would playtest as a better-dressed version of the control-point game the user already rejected.
mustFix: AMPLIFIER IS NOT MOD-DATA — stop treating it as free. Verified Refinery.cs:51 caches IResourceValueModifier from the refinery actor in INotifyCreated.Created and never refreshes; player-scoped capture amplifies nothing and recapture changes nothing. Before relying on it as the anti-second-wallet defense: either (a) write new C# — a player-level IResourceValueModifier that Refinery re-queries per AcceptResources (not cached in Created), scoped as a real ~1-2 day task incl. replay test; or (b) DROP the cash-per-ore amplifier from the first prototype and prove the welded-to-loop thesis with ProductionCostMultiplier instead, which IS a genuine stock per-producer trait gated by a captured prerequisite. Re-label the design: 'amplifiers' = new sim C#, 'cost discounts' = mod-data.

BUILD THE PROTECT LEG BEFORE CLAIMING THE TRIANGLE. GivesBounty is absent from HARV in stock RA. The triangle's third leg is asserted, not real. Add GivesBounty to HARV and playtest harvester raiding as a live, camera-pulling lane on stock RA + 3 zoned ore tiers ALONE. If that micro-test doesn't already feel more RA-tense, no quantity of capturable structures resurrects PROTECT — the triangle is a marketing line and the structures are just a control-point land-grab.

RE-DERIVE THE ECONOMY NUMBERS FROM EARLY-GAME HARVESTER COUNTS (2-4), NOT SATURATED LATE-GAME. The spec's own 14/12/10/6 schedule violates its own 20% territory-cash ceiling at realistic harvester counts. Implement the cap as a LIVE percentage of the player's actual ore rate (a player-level throttle), never a flat cr/s schedule, so it cannot invert when harvester count is low.

FIX THE TWO RIGGED/CONTRADICTORY GATES. (a) Kill-gate #4 must compare camera-time-on-army against STOCK RA WITH the harvester loop (the real game), not the strawman stock-RA-without-the-loop. (b) Re-derive the ignorer floor as WIN-RATE (capture-nothing equal-skill player wins >=~45%), not 0.75 income — income compounds, so 0.75 income is a losing position, not 'weaker but complete.' (c) Replace the self-contradictory ~50/50 attention-neutrality target with an honest 52-55/45-48 edge-to-the-engaged-player, keep the hard >60% mandatory-APM ceiling, and stop claiming the layer is free to ignore.

DECOUPLE SNOWBALL ACCELERANTS FROM COMEBACK GROUND. Do NOT co-locate Radar/Repair/Tech-Center with the richest contested ore. As specced, the leader's vision/detection denies the exact harvester raids the comeback lane depends on — brake and accelerant on the same tile. Separate them, or give every capability node a small universal baseline so no capture is dead and capturing-back is always meaningful.
